ArubaCellular_ArubaModemConfig.description: Cellular uplink configurations for Aruba modem.

aruba-skylark.description: Enables the pre-configured profile for Aruba Skylark LTE modems. When enabled, this creates and activates the ARUBA_USB_LTE profile optimized for Skylark hardware and disables configurations for other modem types. Gateway devices only.

auto-upgrade.description: Automatic firmware upgrade for Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

billing-start-date.description: The day of the month when the cellular billing cycle begins. Used in conjunction with data-rate-limit to track monthly data usage. The data usage counter resets on this date each month.

data-rate-limit.description: The maximum monthly data usage limit for the cellular connection in megabits per second.

frequency.description:
Cellular frequency band configuration for the modem. Groups generation (3G/4G) and
frequency-range settings that together configure the cellular modem's frequency band.

frequency-range.description: The specific radio frequency band to use for cellular communication. Restricting to specific bands can optimize connectivity in regions where certain frequencies have better coverage or performance. Used in conjunction with generation parameter.

generation.description: The cellular technology generation (3G or 4G) used to filter available frequency bands. Used in conjunction with frequency-range to specify precise radio frequency bands for the modem.

gps.description: Enable the GPS on the Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem

internal-lte.description: Enable or disable internal LTE modem. When true, enables internal-lte. When false, disables internal-lte.

modem-apn.description:
Modem APN(Access Point Name) Configuration is used by modem to connect to a mobile network
for internet access, this configuration help the modem identify the correct network and establish a data connection.

apn.description: The Access Point Name (APN) provided by your mobile carrier to establish the data connection. The APN identifies the packet data network (PDN) that the modem should connect to. Valid only when using Aruba modems.

apn-authentication.description: The authentication protocol used to verify credentials with the mobile carrier. Valid only when APN password is configured. Supported values: 0 (No authentication), 1 (PAP - Password Authentication Protocol, sends credentials in clear text), 2 (CHAP - Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol, uses hashed credentials), 3 (MSCHAPv2 - Microsoft CHAP version 2, enhanced security).

modem-e3372.description: Enables the pre-configured profile optimized for Huawei E3372h-320 USB LTE modems. When enabled, the system applies modem-specific initialization and connection parameters. Gateway devices only.

network-mode.description: The preferred cellular network generation for connection. AUTO allows the modem to select the best available technology (3G/4G), while fixed modes (MODE_3G, MODE_4G) restrict connectivity to a specific generation. Forcing a specific mode can improve stability in areas with weak higher-generation signals. Valid only when using Aruba modems. Aruba modems support AUTO, MODE_3G, and MODE_4G.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: the network mode for aruba modem is automatic.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM: Custom mode used by Central UI. Not used for CLI configuration.
x-enumDescriptions.MODE_3G: the network mode for aruba modem is 3G.
x-enumDescriptions.MODE_4G: the network mode for aruba modem is 4G.

network-mode.x-typeDescription: the cellular network mode for Aruba modem.

plmn.description: The Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) identifier used to manually select a specific mobile operator network. PLMN consists of Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC). Valid only when using Aruba modems. Accepts 5-6 digits for AP, GW.

prefer-modem.description: The preferred modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

x-enumDescriptions.NONE: when prefer-modem config is not required.

sim-failover.description: Enables automatic failover between SIM card slots when the active SIM loses connectivity. When enabled, the system will switch to the alternate SIM slot if the primary connection fails, ensuring continuous cellular uplink availability. Applicable to 9004-LTE only.

sim-slot.description: Selects the active SIM card slot (applicable for 9004-LTE only). Use SIM1 or SIM2 to specify which SIM card should be used for cellular connectivity.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: automatic selection of SIM slot.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: when SIM config is not required.

sim-slot.x-typeDescription: the SIM slot for Aruba modem.

internal-lte.description: Enable or disable internal LTE modem. When true, enables internal-lte. When false, disables internal-lte.

modem-apn.description:
Modem APN(Access Point Name) Configuration is used by modem to connect to a mobile network
for internet access, this configuration help the modem identify the correct network and establish a data connection.

apn.description: The Access Point Name (APN) provided by your mobile carrier to establish the data connection. The APN identifies the packet data network (PDN) that the modem should connect to. Valid only when using Aruba modems.

apn-authentication.description: The authentication protocol used to verify credentials with the mobile carrier. Valid only when APN password is configured. Supported values: 0 (No authentication), 1 (PAP - Password Authentication Protocol, sends credentials in clear text), 2 (CHAP - Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol, uses hashed credentials), 3 (MSCHAPv2 - Microsoft CHAP version 2, enhanced security).

modem-e3372.description: Enables the pre-configured profile optimized for Huawei E3372h-320 USB LTE modems. When enabled, the system applies modem-specific initialization and connection parameters. Gateway devices only.

network-mode.description: The preferred cellular network generation for connection. AUTO allows the modem to select the best available technology (3G/4G), while fixed modes (MODE_3G, MODE_4G) restrict connectivity to a specific generation. Forcing a specific mode can improve stability in areas with weak higher-generation signals. Valid only when using Aruba modems. Aruba modems support AUTO, MODE_3G, and MODE_4G.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: the network mode for aruba modem is automatic.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM: Custom mode used by Central UI. Not used for CLI configuration.
x-enumDescriptions.MODE_3G: the network mode for aruba modem is 3G.
x-enumDescriptions.MODE_4G: the network mode for aruba modem is 4G.

network-mode.x-typeDescription: the cellular network mode for Aruba modem.

plmn.description: The Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) identifier used to manually select a specific mobile operator network. PLMN consists of Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC). Valid only when using Aruba modems. Accepts 5-6 digits for AP, GW.

prefer-modem.description: The preferred modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

x-enumDescriptions.NONE: when prefer-modem config is not required.

sim-failover.description: Enables automatic failover between SIM card slots when the active SIM loses connectivity. When enabled, the system will switch to the alternate SIM slot if the primary connection fails, ensuring continuous cellular uplink availability. Applicable to 9004-LTE only.

sim-slot.description: Selects the active SIM card slot (applicable for 9004-LTE only). Use SIM1 or SIM2 to specify which SIM card should be used for cellular connectivity.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: automatic selection of SIM slot.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: when SIM config is not required.

assignment-rules.description:
Assign the client a user role, VLAN ID or VLAN name based on attributes. For GW and AP, the attributes is returned for the client by the authentication server and this API is applicable for
auth server group. For AP, this API is also applicable WLAN profile and if this API works in WLAN profile, the attributes can be returned for the client by the authentication server or other
attributes such as mac-address, dhcp-option, AP-Name, etc. Rules are ordered: the first rule that matches the configured condition is applied. VLAN IDs and VLAN names cannot be listed together.
This feature is only applicable for AP and GW.

attribute.description:
Attribute returned by the authentication server.
For AP, it also includes some custom attributes like mac-address, dhcp-option and fw_mode.

interface-mode.description:
Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan and trunk-vlan-ranges should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

native-vlan.description:
Native VLAN id for untagged frames arriving on
a trunk interface.  Tagged frames sent on an interface
configured with a native VLAN should have their tags
stripped prior to transmission. This configuration is only
valid on a trunk interface.

specified as x-y where x and y are valid VLAN IDs
(1 <= vlan-id <= 4094). The range is assumed to be inclusive,
such that any VLAN-ID matching x <= VLAN-ID <= y falls within
the range.

for 4100i, 5420, 6000, 6100, 6200, 6300 and 6400 platforms.

error-control.description:
Forward Error Correction (FEC). Add redundant bits to a data stream
enabling the receiver to detect and correct transmission errors.

and only when linked at 100Mbps. It has no effect at other speeds or on other ports. Supported primarily on

lower than expected speed and should not be used on ports that are members of a LAG.

unknown-vlans.description:
Configure GVRP unknown VLANs handling mode for ethernet interface.
 Learn: Accept join requests for new VLANs and propagate through GVRP.
 Block: Process GVRP packets for known VLANs only, ignore new VLANs.
 Disable: Ignore all GVRP packets.

x-enumDescriptions.BLOCK:
Only process GVRP packets that concern themselves with
 known VLANs and ignore new VLANs.
x-enumDescriptions.DISABLE: Ignore all GVRP packets.
x-enumDescriptions.LEARN:
Accept join requests for new VLANs on this port and
 propagate requests through all other forwarding ports
 that are participating in GVRP.

Enable speed downshift for 1000BASE-T port. This is a non-standard mode for use only when standards-based
auto-negotiation is not able to establish a stable link. Enabling this may cause the port to link at a
lower than expected speed and should not be used on ports that are members of a LAG.

unknown-vlans.description:
Configure GVRP unknown VLANs handling mode for ethernet interface.
 Learn: Accept join requests for new VLANs and propagate through GVRP.
 Block: Process GVRP packets for known VLANs only, ignore new VLANs.
 Disable: Ignore all GVRP packets.

x-enumDescriptions.BLOCK:
Only process GVRP packets that concern themselves with
 known VLANs and ignore new VLANs.
x-enumDescriptions.DISABLE: Ignore all GVRP packets.
x-enumDescriptions.LEARN:
Accept join requests for new VLANs on this port and
 propagate requests through all other forwarding ports
 that are participating in GVRP.

poe.description:
Power-over-ethernet(PoE) configurations.
The power-over-ethernet (PoE) manages the power supplied to
devices using standard Ethernet data cables.

allocation-method.description:
Power allocation method. By default, power allocation is automatic based on device usage.
Allowed configurable values are 'usage' or 'class' or 'value'

assigned-class.description:
Limit PoE power based on the assigned class.
Class 3 (13W max at powered device (PD))
Class 4 (25.5W max at powered device (PD))
Class 6 (51W max at  powered device (PD))
Class 8 (71.3W max at  powered device (PD))

cycle-timeout.description: Timeout value in units of seconds to control POE power delivery.

enabled.description:
Enable/Disable power-over-ethernet on the interface.
PoE on each port can be Enabled/Disabled individually.

lldp-detect.description:
Allow the link partner to specify power allocation using LLDP.
By default, LLDP power information is ignored.

pd-class-override.description:
The pd-class-override enables a device to draw power more than the
the power limit specified in IEEE classification.
By default,it is disabled. Power allocation method should be set
to 'class' when override needs to be enabled.

poe-cisco.description: Enable or disable PoE Cisco in the ethernet interface.

power-pairs.description:
Configure what cable pairs deliver power.
A 2-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on just one pairset, Alt-A or Alt-B.
A 4-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on both pairsets Alt-A and Alt-B

x-enumDescriptions.ALT_A: Delivers power only on the ALT-A pair.
x-enumDescriptions.ALT_A_AND_B: Delivers power on the ALT-A and ALT-B pairs.

power-pairs.x-typeDescription: Configure what cable pairs deliver power.

pre-std-detect.description:
Enable detection of pre-standard PoE devices. When 'pre-std-detect' is enabled,
power will be delivered on 'alt-a' pair only. By default 'pre-std-detect' is disabled.

priority.description:
Configure PoE priority in the event of power over-subscription.
Configurable values for priority on the interface are low, critical or high. Default priority is low

value.description:
Set the maximum power allocation for the port.
Applicable only when 'poe-allocate-by' is set to 'value'.

origin.description:
A port with a VLAN translation configuration allows traffic only for the translated VLAN and the native VLAN;
if it is a member of more VLANS, it does not allow traffic for them.
A translated VLAN must be present on the switch before the rule is created; the original VLAN need not be present.
VLAN translation and MVRP cannot be enabled on the same interface.

interface.description: Represents a single physical Ethernet or USB interface configuration on the device. Each interface is uniquely identified by its name (e.g., 0/0/1, enet0, usb0). Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete an interface configuration instance.

alternate-linkup.description: Enables Direct Attach Copper (DAC) alternate link detection mechanism for improved cable compatibility. This feature helps resolve link-up issues with certain DAC cables by using an alternative link establishment method. Useful for troubleshooting connectivity problems with passive copper cables. Corresponds to the dac-alternate-linkup command on gateway devices.

ap-profile.description: AP Port Profile (if any) associated with the interface.

br-profile.description: BRIDGE Port Profile (if any) associated with the interface.

description.description:
Description of the interface.
AOS-CX: length: 1-64

duplex.description: Configures the duplex mode for the Ethernet interface. Full-duplex allows simultaneous bidirectional communication for maximum throughput. Half-duplex only permits one direction at a time and is rarely used in modern networks. Auto-negotiation (default) automatically selects the best duplex mode supported by both devices. Manual settings must match on both ends of the link to avoid connectivity issues.

items.description: Forbid vlans for interface.
items.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

gw-profile.description: References an existing Gateway Port Profile to apply centrally managed port policies to this interface. Gateway profiles provide template-based configuration for firewall rules, AAA settings, and other gateway-specific features. When assigned, profile settings override local interface configurations unless the retain-profile-configs option is enabled.

isolated-vlans.description: Isolated VLAN ID for the interface.

items.description: Isolated VLAN ID for the interface.
items.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

jumbo-mtu.description: Enables support for Jumbo frames (Ethernet frames larger than the standard 1500-byte MTU, typically up to 9000 bytes). Jumbo frames improve network throughput and reduce CPU overhead for large data transfers such as storage traffic, backups, and virtualization workloads. All devices in the network path must support Jumbo frames to prevent fragmentation. Corresponds to the jumbo command on gateway devices.

name.description: Unique identifier for the Ethernet or USB interface. Supported formats include slot-based naming (e.g., 0/0/1 for slot 0, module 0, port 1) and logical naming (e.g., enet0, usb0). Device models enforce specific port ranges through capability constraints (e.g., gateway model GW_7005 supports 0/0/[0-3], GW_7205 supports 0/0/[0-5]). This field is mandatory and serves as the primary key for the interface instance.

port-monitor.description: Configures this interface as a monitoring port that receives mirrored traffic from another source interface (SPAN/port mirroring). The source can be a physical GigabitEthernet interface or a Port-Channel/LAG. All traffic from the source interface is duplicated and sent to this monitoring port for analysis, troubleshooting, or security monitoring purposes. Gateway devices only.

enable.description: Enables or disables port monitoring (SPAN/traffic mirroring) on this interface. When enabled, this interface receives a copy of all traffic from the specified source interface for analysis. Operational constraints: Only one monitoring session can be active on the device at a time. LLDP must be disabled on the monitoring port (enforced by system). Neither the monitoring port nor the monitored source port can be part of a Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) group or port-channel. The source interface must be different from the monitoring interface. Use this for network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, or security monitoring.

src-interface-id.description: Identifies the source interface to be monitored. For physical ports, use slot/module/port format (e.g., 0/0/1). For port-channels, use the LAG number (e.g., 5). This must be different from the monitoring interface identifier to prevent loops. The system enforces that source and destination interfaces cannot be the same.

src-interface-type.description: Specifies the type of source interface whose traffic will be mirrored to this monitoring port. GIGABIT_ETHERNET mirrors traffic from a single physical Ethernet port. PORT_CHANNEL mirrors aggregated traffic from all member ports in a Link Aggregation Group (LAG).

x-enumDescriptions.GIGABIT_ETHERNET: Source interface is a physical GigabitEthernet port. Traffic from this port will be mirrored to the monitoring interface.
x-enumDescriptions.PORT_CHANNEL: Source interface is a Link Aggregation Group (LAG/Port-Channel). Aggregated traffic from all member ports will be mirrored.

src-interface-type.x-typeDescription: Defines the type of network interface that will be monitored (source) for traffic mirroring purposes. Gateway devices only.

port-type.description: Designates the interface as either a WAN (Wide Area Network) or LAN (Local Area Network) port. WAN ports typically connect to external networks or service providers and may apply different security policies, NAT rules, and routing behaviors. LAN ports connect to internal trusted networks. This designation affects firewall rules, routing decisions, and security policy enforcement.
port-type.x-typeDescription: For microbranch AP, port type WAN means uplink, port type LAN means downlink

portchannel-lag.description: Attach a link aggreagatioin group (LAG) to physical interface.

retain-profile-configs.description:
To decide whether or not to retain profile configs on an interface when
the profile is removed from the said interface

speed.description: Configures the link speed for the Ethernet interface. When set to SPEED_AUTO (default), the interface automatically negotiates the highest supported speed with the connected device. Manual speed settings force the interface to operate at a specific rate, which may require matching configuration on the peer device.

speed-mode.description: Configures the operational speed mode for multi-rate capable interfaces. Only supported on 7280 hardware. Determines whether the interface operates in 40Gbps, 10Gbps, or 1Gbps mode. Changing this setting may affect port availability or require a reboot. Consult hardware documentation for supported speed modes per interface.

sw-profile.description: Switch Port Profile (if any) associated with the interface.

trusted.description: Marks the interface as trusted for security policy purposes. Trusted interfaces bypass certain security checks and firewall rules, allowing unrestricted communication. Typically applied to internal management interfaces or connections to known secure networks. Use with caution as this reduces security enforcement on the interface.

tunneled-node-port.description: Enables tunneled node functionality on the interface, allowing it to participate in overlay network tunneling. When enabled, traffic received on this port can be automatically encapsulated and forwarded through SD-WAN or VPN tunnels based on routing policies. Typically used for branch office deployments where local devices need transparent access to central resources over secure tunnels.

ArubaInterfaceEthernet_EthernetInterface.description: Ethernet interfaces provide physical connectivity for network devices including switches, gateways, access points, and bridges. This module supports configuration of interface properties, port profiles, link aggregation, Power over Ethernet (PoE), security features (AAA, port-security, LLDP), Layer 3 routing capabilities, and advanced features like PIM multicast, flow telemetry, and port monitoring. Supported scopes: Device. This configuration relies on Port Profile configurations (sw-profile for switches, gw-profile for gateways, ap-profile for access points, br-profile for bridges) for template-based settings. Interface names follow device-specific patterns (e.g., gateway model GW_7005 supports 0/0/[0-3], GW_7205 supports 0/0/[0-5]). Use this API to retrieve the list of Ethernet Interface configurations.

alternate-linkup.description: Enables Direct Attach Copper (DAC) alternate link detection mechanism for improved cable compatibility. This feature helps resolve link-up issues with certain DAC cables by using an alternative link establishment method. Useful for troubleshooting connectivity problems with passive copper cables. Corresponds to the dac-alternate-linkup command on gateway devices.

aos-s-switch-model.description:
The model type of the AOS-S switch. This specifies the physical model identifier
       for switches across different form factors and capabilities. Each model
       type corresponds to a specific hardware platform with predetermined port
       counts, uplink configurations, and features like PoE support. This leaf
       is used to target Interface Profile configurations to specific hardware models.
       This field cannot be edited once created.

ArubaInterfaceProfile_AossStackCustomGro.description:
A grouping for defining custom stack configurations with detailed member information.
This grouping enables the creation of heterogeneous switch stacks with specific member counts,
varying port types, and individual Interface Profiles for each member. Unlike automatic stack
configurations that apply a uniform configuration across identical stack members, this
custom grouping allows for precise control over each stack member's configuration, supporting
deployments with mixed switch models or varying port requirements across the stack.

aos-s-member-count.description:
The total number of switch members in the custom stack configuration. This value
determines how many switches will be managed as a single logical entity in the stack.
The range is limited to 0-10 members, where 0 indicates an empty stack definition
that can be populated later, and values 1-10 represent the actual number of physical
switches in the stack.

aos-s-members.description:
A list containing configuration details for individual switch members in the stack.
Each entry represents a single physical switch with its own member ID, port configuration,
and Interface Profile references. This allows for heterogeneous stack configurations where
different switch models can be combined into a single managed stack. The list is limited
to a maximum of 10 elements, matching the maximum supported stack size.

aos-s-member-id.description:
The unique identifier for a member switch within the stack. This ID serves as
the primary key for identifying individual switches in the stack configuration.
Valid values range from 0 to 10, corresponding to the physical position or
assigned ID of each switch in the stack topology.

ArubaInterfaceProfile_AossStackCustomGro.description:
A grouping for defining custom stack configurations with detailed member information.
This grouping enables the creation of heterogeneous switch stacks with specific member counts,
varying port types, and individual Interface Profiles for each member. Unlike automatic stack
configurations that apply a uniform configuration across identical stack members, this
custom grouping allows for precise control over each stack member's configuration, supporting
deployments with mixed switch models or varying port requirements across the stack.

aos-s-member-count.description:
The total number of switch members in the custom stack configuration. This value
determines how many switches will be managed as a single logical entity in the stack.
The range is limited to 0-10 members, where 0 indicates an empty stack definition
that can be populated later, and values 1-10 represent the actual number of physical
switches in the stack.

aos-s-members.description:
A list containing configuration details for individual switch members in the stack.
Each entry represents a single physical switch with its own member ID, port configuration,
and Interface Profile references. This allows for heterogeneous stack configurations where
different switch models can be combined into a single managed stack. The list is limited
to a maximum of 10 elements, matching the maximum supported stack size.

aos-s-member-id.description:
The unique identifier for a member switch within the stack. This ID serves as
the primary key for identifying individual switches in the stack configuration.
Valid values range from 0 to 10, corresponding to the physical position or
assigned ID of each switch in the stack topology.

specified, separated by commas. Example: 0/0/0,0/0/1-0/0/3,0/0/4

ArubaInterfaceProfile_InterfaceProfilesS.description:
List of Interface Profile configuration. Interface Profile is bundle of interface configuration
for devices with specific sku/model. Defined for set of uplink/downlink ports for given models.
Interface Profile can be defined for stacks/chassis for fixed/automatic set of members/LineCards.
Interface Profile can be defined for custom stack/chassis size.
One Interface Profile can have port-profile config for uplink + downlink + custom ports for given
model/device type. In case of stacks, Interface Profile will not be applied VSF link ports, if they
are part of automatic/custom Interface Profile model+ports.

interface-profile.description:
Interface Profile configuration. It is a bundle of interface configuration
for devices with specific sku/model. Defined for set of uplink/downlink ports, or can
be for custom set of ports for given models. Interface Profile can be defined for stacks/chassis for
fixed/automatic set of members/LineCards. Interface Profile can be defined for custom stack/chassis size.
One Interface Profile can have port-profile config for uplink + downlink + custom ports for given
model/device type. In case of stacks, Interface Profile will not be applied VSF link ports, if they
are part of automatic/custom Interface Profile model+ports.

aos-s-switch-chassis-automatic.description:
Automatic Interface Profile configuration for chassis switches with modules. This container provides a
simplified configuration approach for chassis switches, applying consistent Interface Profile
settings across all installed line cards. It is ideal for homogeneous chassis
deployments where all modules serve similar functions in the network.

aos-s-switch-chassis-custom.description:
Custom Interface Profile configuration for chassis switches with modules. This container enables
precise control over interface settings for each line card in a chassis switch.
It supports advanced network designs where different modules may require specialized
configurations based on their position, connectivity, or functional role.

aos-s-switch-linecard.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines linecard switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

aos-s-switch-member.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines member switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across member switch deployments with specific hardware models.

aos-s-switch-modular.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines standalone switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

aos-s-switch-stack-automatic.description:
Switch stack automatic port grouping. This container enables uniform Interface Profile configuration
across all members in a switch stack with identical hardware. It simplifies management
by allowing administrators to define a single configuration that is automatically
applied to all stack members, ensuring consistent behavior across the stack.

aos-s-switch-stack-custom.description:
Switch stack custom port grouping. This container supports heterogeneous stack
configurations by allowing different Interface Profiles for each member in the stack.
It provides granular control over interface settings for each stack member,
accommodating different hardware models or functional roles within the stack.

aos-s-switch-standalone.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines standalone switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

ap.description:
Interface Profile configuration for AP. This container enables
precise control over interface settings for each port.

device-type.x-typeDescription: Interface Profile applied to device types.

gateway-standalone.description:
Gateway port grouping. This container defines gateway configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for ports. It provides a
comprehensive framework for applying consistent port settings across gateway deployments with
specific hardware models.

pvos-switch-chassis-automatic.description:
Automatic Interface Profile configuration for chassis switches with modules. This container provides a
simplified configuration approach for chassis switches, applying consistent Interface Profile
settings across all installed line cards. It is ideal for homogeneous chassis
deployments where all modules serve similar functions in the network.

pvos-switch-chassis-custom.description:
Custom Interface Profile configuration for chassis switches with modules. This container enables
precise control over interface settings for each line card in a chassis switch.
It supports advanced network designs where different modules may require specialized
configurations based on their position, connectivity, or functional role.

pvos-switch-linecard.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines linecard switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

pvos-switch-member.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines member switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across member switch deployments with specific hardware models.

pvos-switch-stack-automatic.description:
Switch stack automatic port grouping. This container enables uniform Interface Profile configuration
across all members in a switch stack with identical hardware. It simplifies management
by allowing administrators to define a single configuration that is automatically
applied to all stack members, ensuring consistent behavior across the stack.

pvos-switch-stack-custom.description:
Switch stack custom port grouping. This container supports heterogeneous stack
configurations by allowing different Interface Profiles for each member in the stack.
It provides granular control over interface settings for each stack member,
accommodating different hardware models or functional roles within the stack.

pvos-switch-standalone.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines standalone switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

switch-linecard.description:

It supports advanced network designs where different modules may require specialized
configurations based on their position, connectivity, or functional role.

switch-stack-automatic.description:
Switch stack automatic port grouping. This container enables uniform Interface Profile configuration
across all members in a switch stack with identical hardware. It simplifies management

applied to all stack members, ensuring consistent behavior across the stack.

switch-stack-custom.description:
Switch stack custom port grouping. This container supports heterogeneous stack
configurations by allowing different Interface Profiles for each member in the stack.
It provides granular control over interface settings for each stack member,
accommodating different hardware models or functional roles within the stack.

switch-standalone.description:
Switch port grouping. This container defines standalone switch configurations,
including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent
port settings across standalone switch deployments with specific hardware models.

switch-vsx-modular.description:
VSX Modular Interface Profile configuration. This container enables configuration
of VSX pairs with chassis/modular switches, providing redundancy and high availability
with full line-card support. Both Peer1 and Peer2 must use matching VSX-supported
chassis models (5420, 6405, 6410, 8400). Exception: 6405 and 6410 models can be paired
together. Each peer can have independent line-card configurations while maintaining
compatible hardware models.

modular-peer1.description:
Configuration for VSX Peer1 modular/chassis switch. This peer represents the primary
device in a VSX pair configuration for chassis-based switches with line cards.
Supported VSX chassis models: 5420, 6405, 6410, 8400.

modular-peer2.description:
Configuration for VSX Peer2 modular/chassis switch. This peer represents the secondary
device in a VSX pair configuration. Both peers must have matching switch models, with
the exception that 6405 and 6410 models can be paired together.
Supported VSX chassis models: 5420, 6405, 6410, 8400.

switch-vsx-standalone.description:
VSX Standalone Interface Profile configuration. This container enables configuration
of VSX pairs with standalone switches, providing redundancy and high availability.
Both Peer1 and Peer2 must use matching VSX-supported standalone models (6300, 8100,
8320, 8325, 8360, 8400, 9300, 10000). Each peer can have independent port profiles
while maintaining consistent hardware models.

peer1.description:
Configuration for VSX Peer1 standalone switch. This peer represents the primary
device in a VSX pair configuration.

peer2.description:
Configuration for VSX Peer2 standalone switch. This peer represents the secondary
device in a VSX pair configuration. Both peers must have matching switch models.

including model specification, port types, and interface mappings for both uplink
and downlink ports. It provides a comprehensive framework for applying consistent

switch-vsx-modular.description:

with full line-card support. Both Peer1 and Peer2 must use matching VSX-supported
chassis models (5420, 6405, 6410, 8400). Exception: 6405 and 6410 models can be paired
together. Each peer can have independent line-card configurations while maintaining
compatible hardware models.

modular-peer1.description:

modular-peer2.description:

the exception that 6405 and 6410 models can be paired together.

switch-vsx-standalone.description:

of VSX pairs with standalone switches, providing redundancy and high availability.
Both Peer1 and Peer2 must use matching VSX-supported standalone models (6300, 8100,
8320, 8325, 8360, 8400, 9300, 10000). Each peer can have independent port profiles
while maintaining consistent hardware models.

peer1.description:

peer2.description:

ArubaInterfaceProfile_PvosStackCustomGro.description:
A grouping for defining custom stack configurations with detailed member information.
This grouping enables the creation of heterogeneous switch stacks with specific member counts,
varying port types, and individual Interface Profiles for each member. Unlike automatic stack
configurations that apply a uniform configuration across identical stack members, this
custom grouping allows for precise control over each stack member's configuration, supporting
deployments with mixed switch models or varying port requirements across the stack.

pvos-member-count.description:
The total number of switch members in the custom stack configuration. This value
determines how many switches will be managed as a single logical entity in the stack.
The range is limited to 0-10 members, where 0 indicates an empty stack definition
that can be populated later, and values 1-10 represent the actual number of physical
switches in the stack.

pvos-members.description:
A list containing configuration details for individual switch members in the stack.
Each entry represents a single physical switch with its own member ID, port configuration,
and Interface Profile references. This allows for heterogeneous stack configurations where
different switch models can be combined into a single managed stack. The list is limited
to a maximum of 10 elements, matching the maximum supported stack size.

pvos-member-id.description:
The unique identifier for a member switch within the stack. This ID serves as
the primary key for identifying individual switches in the stack configuration.
Valid values range from 0 to 10, corresponding to the physical position or
assigned ID of each switch in the stack topology.

the range. Example 1,2-3,4

ArubaInterfaceProfile_StackCustomGroupin.description:
A grouping for defining custom stack configurations with detailed member information.
This grouping enables the creation of heterogeneous switch stacks with specific member counts,
varying port types, and individual Interface Profiles for each member. Unlike automatic stack
configurations that apply a uniform configuration across identical stack members, this
custom grouping allows for precise control over each stack member's configuration, supporting
deployments with mixed switch models or varying port requirements across the stack.

member-count.description:
The total number of switch members in the custom stack configuration. This value
determines how many switches will be managed as a single logical entity in the stack.
The range is limited to 0-10 members, where 0 indicates an empty stack definition
that can be populated later, and values 1-10 represent the actual number of physical
switches in the stack.

members.description:
A list containing configuration details for individual switch members in the stack.
Each entry represents a single physical switch with its own member ID, port configuration,
and Interface Profile references. This allows for heterogeneous stack configurations where
different switch models can be combined into a single managed stack. The list is limited
to a maximum of 10 elements, matching the maximum supported stack size.

member-id.description:
The unique identifier for a member switch within the stack. This ID serves as
the primary key for identifying individual switches in the stack configuration.
Valid values range from 0 to 10, corresponding to the physical position or
assigned ID of each switch in the stack topology.

treatment of uplink and downlink ports. It enables the application of specific profiles

downlink-port-map.description:
List of all the downlink ports and associated port-profiles references.
User's discretion is required to fill the downlink port range.
No validation is performed to verify whether given port range is uplink/downlink ports

downlink-port.description: Comma separated downlink Ports/range in format 1,2-4.
downlink-port.x-typeDescription:
Comma separated list of PORT IDs and ranges.
PortID or only single-tagged PortIDs or both. A range is
specified as x-y where x and y are valid Port IDs
(1 <= port-id <= 64). The range is assumed to be inclusive,
such that any Port-ID matching x <= Port-ID <= y falls within
the range. Example 1,2-3,4

uplink-port-map.description:

is performed to verify whether given port range is uplink ports

ArubaInterfaceQos_FlowControlConfig.description:
The interface's 802.3x or priority-based flow-control configuration. On
some platforms, memory pools must first be configured (using the
aruba-qos-pool yang model) before any interface flow-control configuration
will take effect.

cable-length.description:
Specifies the cable-length auto-detection mode or the value
 in meters used to compute the headroom limit for lossless traffic
 arriving on the interface. The default value is 350 meters.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: Automatically detect cable-length.

flow-control-mode.description:
Flow-control mode for the interface: Link Level Flow Control (LLFC),
Priority Flow Control (PFC), or none. On some platforms, memory pools
must first be configured (using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) before
any interface flow-control configuration will take effect.
flow-control-mode.x-typeDescription:
Specifies the type of flow control to apply - Link Level
Flow Control (LLFC), Priority Flow Control (PFC), or none.

llfc-flow-control.description:
Configuration for 802.3x link-level flow control (LLFC). On some
platforms, a memory pool must first be created (using the
aruba-qos-pool yang model) that matches the llfc-pool-id value before
any 802.3X link-level Tx or RxTx flow-control configuration will
take effect.

direction.description:
This mandatory field specifies whether the interface is enabled to
handle received flow-control frames, to transmit flow-control frames,
or both. This setting only applies to 802.3X link-level flow control.

x-enumDescriptions.RX: Respond to receiving a flow-control pause frame from the link peer.
x-enumDescriptions.RXTX:
Transmit bi-directional flow-control pause frames to the link peer and
respond to received flow-control pause frames from the link peer.
x-enumDescriptions.TX: Transmit flow-control pause frames to the link peer.

direction.x-typeDescription: Specifies the direction(s) in which flow control will be applied.

llfc-pool-id.description:
The pool ID for arriving lossless LLFC packets. On some platforms, a
memory pool with the same pool ID value must first be configured
(using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) before any 802.3X link-level Tx
or RxTx flow-control configuration will take effect.

override-negotiation.description:
Enables overriding link-negotiation results and using
the locally-specified flow-control mode instead.

lossless-buffer-based-link-level-flow-co.description: Buffer threshold configuration for 802.3x link-level flow control, including XOF and XON limits, headroom, and other parameters.

lossless-buffer-based-priority-flow-cont.description:
Buffer threshold configuration for 802.1Qbb priority flow control,
including XOFF and XON limits, headroom, and other parameters.

thresholds.description: Buffer-configuration threshold specific to each PFC priority.

priority.description: Packet priority value from the 802.1Q VLAN header.

pfc-watchdog.description:
Enables the priority flow control watchdog. The watchdog detects when
flow-controlled egress queues are paused for an excessive duration, and
takes action when the globally-configured trigger time has elapsed with
the queue remaining paused.

priority-config.description: Per-priority direction and buffer configuration for priority flow control.

direction.description:
This mandatory field specifies whether the interface priority is
enabled to handle received priority flow-control frames, transmit
priority flow-control frames, or both.

x-enumDescriptions.RX: Respond to receiving a flow-control pause frame from the link peer.
x-enumDescriptions.RXTX:
Transmit bi-directional flow-control pause frames to the link peer and
respond to received flow-control pause frames from the link peer.
x-enumDescriptions.TX: Transmit flow-control pause frames to the link peer.

direction.x-typeDescription: Specifies the direction(s) in which flow control will be applied.

priority.description:
Packet priority value found in the 802.1Q VLAN header. On some
platforms, one or more memory pools must first be created (using the
aruba-qos-pool yang model) and have the desired priorities assigned
to them before any Priority Flow Control (PFC) configuration will
take effect.

modify, or delete a VLAN interface.

IP routing functionality for VLANs, enabling inter-VLAN routing and
gateway services. VLAN interfaces support IPv4/IPv6 addressing, DHCP

3 IPv6 addresses, 16 IPv4 helper addresses, and 3 IPv6 helper
addresses per VLAN interface. Use this API to retrieve the list of
VLAN interfaces.

ArubaLacp_LacpSchema.description:
Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) dynamically negotiates and
manages link aggregation groups (LAGs/Port Channels) per IEEE
802.3ad/802.1AX standards. LACP provides automatic failover, load
distribution across member links, and detection of misconfigured
aggregation. Configure system-level LACP priority, hashing algorithms,
and interface-specific parameters including active/passive modes,
heartbeat rates (fast/slow), and minimum active link thresholds. Use
this API to retrieve LACP system configuration.

system-priority.description: System priority used in LACP negotiation.

ArubaLldp_LldpSchemaGET.description:
The Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is an industry-standard,
vendor-neutral method to allow networked devices to advertise capabilities,
discover and identify other LLDP enabled devices and gather information in a
LAN. LLDP is supported on physical interfaces and Out-Of-Band Management (OOBM)
interfaces and it is not supported on logical interfaces.

ArubaSwPortProfile_SwPortProfilesSchemaG.description:
Configure and manage port profiles.
A port profile is a template for configuring ethernet interface configurations.
It is a mechanism intended to ease the process of configuring multiple interfaces
with same set of configurations. Instead of manually configuring each interface one-by-one,
the port profile collects the common configuration settings and allows them to be applied on
the interface or a collection of interfaces.

ArubaUfd_UfdSchemaGET.description:
Uplink Failure Detection(UFD) Configurations.UFD monitors (tracks the forwarding state of)
the interfaces/LAGs(Link Aggregation) configured as links-to-monitor (LtM) and when all
LtM links go down,UFD disables the interfaces/LAGs configured as links-to-disable (LtD).
If any of the LtM links come back up, then all the LtD links are brought back up

UFD disables the interfaces/LAGs configured as links-to-disable.

configured under links-to-monitor.

machine-auth.description:
Configure a machine authentication rule. When a Windows device boots, it logs onto the network domain using a machine account. Within the domain, the device is authenticated
before computer group policies and software settings can be executed; this process is known as machine authentication. Machine authentication ensures that only authorized devices
are allowed on the network. You can configure 802.1X for both user and machine authentication. This tightens the authentication process further, since both the device and user need
to be authenticated. This feature is applicable for 802.1x authenticaion and it is only applicable for AP.

Config the global profile for USB parameters. Including a usb profile list and the acl rule profiles detail.
a AP USB ACL profile policy including a acl-name and a rule list. The rule includes a USB vendor name and
its related action is deny or permit. Such as vendor is Alcatel-L800, action is deny, it means the Alcatel-L800

bridging-mode.description:
Configure Bridging mode for VXLAN.
By default, packets arriving on an L2VNI over a VXLAN tunnel are not forwarded
to another VXLAN tunnel on the same L2VNI. This behavior is known as DENY.
Set the mode to static-evpn to allow communication between static tunnels and dynamic tunnels.
Set the mode to static-all to enable bridging between static tunnels and any other static or dynamic tunnels.

x-enumDescriptions.DENY: Disable traffic bridging between VXLAN tunnels on same L2VNI.
x-enumDescriptions.STATIC_ALL: Enable traffic bridging between all VXLAN tunnels on same L2VNI.
x-enumDescriptions.STATIC_EVPN: Enable traffic bridging between static and dynamic VXLAN tunnels on same L2VNI.

enable-counters.description:
Enable Aggregate counters for VXLAN.
It records aggregate statistics for packets being sent or received on VXLAN.

loop-protect.description:
Enable loop-protect on VXLAN, to identify and prevent accidental loops in a network.
Loop-protect is applicable only for IPV4 VXLAN.

loop-protect-vlans.description:
Configure VLANs to be considered for sending loop-protect pdus for a port.
It is applicable only for IPV4 VXLAN.

It is applicable only for IPV4 VXLAN.

ArubaInterfaceVxlan_VxlanSchemaGET.description:
Configure VXLAN. Virtual eXtensible Local Access Network (VXLAN)
provides a framework for Overlaying Virtualized Layer 2 Networks
over Layer 3 networks. In CX it creates a VXLAN Interface.

profile.description:
Global profile for VXLAN configuration parameters,
each scope (global, site, site-collection, device, device-collection)
can accept only one profile. This profile creates VXLAN Interface in AOS-CX.
This list is deprecated now, please use the configuration from aruba-interface-vni.yang

description.description: Configure user description for VXLAN profile.

vni.description:
Configure VNI(s) for VXLAN.
A VNI represents a VXLAN segment and extends the broadcast
domain represented by a VLAN. AOS-CX supports asymmetric routing
by default, symmetric routing is enabled by associating the
VNI with a VRF instead of a VLAN.

id.description: Configure Virtual network identifier for VXLAN.

policy-name.description:
Configure Policy for on VNI.
A policy can be applied only if VRF is configured and routing is enabled on the VNI.

symmetric-routing.description:
Enable symmetric routing for VNI.
Routing cannot be enabled on a VNI that is associated with a VLAN.

vlan.description:
Configure VLAN to VNI. Only one VLAN can be associated with VNI.
VLAN to VNI association is not allowed on a VNI that has symmetric routing enabled or is associated with VRF.
vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

vrf.description:
Configure VRF for VNI for symmetric routing.
VNI to VRF association is not allowed on a VNI that is associated with a VLAN.
vrf.x-typeDescription: Type definition for 'name', should be alphanumeric. Special characters such as '\', '/' and space are not allowed.

domain.x-typeDescription:
The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

ArubaNamedCondition_NamedConditionGroup.description:
Configuration data for traffic classification rule conditions.
This configuration defines the specific criteria used to match and classify network
traffic for policy enforcement. It provides a flexible framework for combining
multiple classification methods including application-based, transport-layer,
IP-layer, and Ethernet-layer conditions.

The conditional inclusion of different field types allows for optimal rule
configuration based on the classification needs:
- Service conditions: Application and DPI-based classification
- Transport fields: TCP/UDP port and protocol information
- IP protocol fields: Network layer addressing and protocol data
- Ethernet fields: Layer 2 MAC addressing and VLAN information

ArubaNamedCondition_NamedConditionsSchem.description:
Named Condition describes a Traffic Class on device.
Named conditions serve as reusable traffic classification templates that
can be referenced by multiple policies across the system.

named-condition.description:
Individual named condition (Traffic Class) configuration entry.
Each named condition represents a specific traffic classification rule
that can be applied to network policies. The condition defines criteria
for matching network traffic based on various protocol headers and
application characteristics.

Named conditions provide reusability and consistency across multiple
policies, allowing network administrators to define traffic classes
once and reference them in various policy contexts such as network,
access control, and QoS.

association.description:
Association context for the named condition, defining the scope and application
domain where this traffic classification rule will be active. The association
type determines how the named condition integrates with different policy
network contexts within the system.

Association types typically include interface-specific or
role-based contexts, allowing for control over where traffic classification
rules are applied.

condition-rule.description:
Ordered list of traffic classification rules that collectively define the
named condition (Traffic Class). Each rule specifies matching criteria for
network traffic using various protocol headers and application characteristics.

All rules within this list must conform to the same classification type
as specified in the parent named condition's rules-type field.

count.description: Enable packet counting for traffic matching this rule.

description.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for this rule entry.

ignore.description:
When set to true, this rule is ignored during traffic
classification processing and no further action will be taken except
for log and count.

log.description:
Enable logging for traffic matching this rule when used in access control contexts.
This option is available only for network ACL rule types (Ethernet, IP, IPv6).
When enabled, matching traffic events are recorded in the system logs, providing
audit trails for security monitoring and troubleshooting.

position.description:
Sequential position number for this rule within the named condition's rule list.
Position determines the order of rule evaluation, with lower numbers processed
first. This ordering is critical for traffic classification logic where multiple
rules might match the same traffic flow. Position values must be unique within
the named condition and should allow.

description.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for the Named Condition (Traffic Class).

name.description:
Unique identifier for the named condition, which becomes the Traffic Class name
on the device. This name must be unique within the system and follows standard
naming conventions for network device objects. The Traffic Class name is used
by policies to reference this traffic classification rule.

reverse-named-condition.description:
Boolean flag to enable reverse functionality for role-based policies.
When enabled, this creates bidirectional traffic classification for role-based
access control, allowing policies to automatically apply matching rules in
both directions of communication flows.

rules-type.description:
Classification type for the named condition, determining which protocol layers
and fields are available for traffic matching.

Available types include:
- IP-based conditions: Match on network layer protocols and addressing
- Ethernet-based conditions: Match on data link layer MAC and VLAN information
- Application-based conditions: Match on identified applications and services

All rules within a single named condition must use the same classification type.

ArubaNamedCondition_NamedServiceGroup.description:
Configuration data for application and service-based traffic classification.
Named Service Group defines the criteria for matching network traffic based on
application categories and specific.

Application categories provide broad classification of traffic types (e.g., social media,
video streaming, business applications), while specific applications identify
individual protocols or services (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, specific SaaS applications).

ArubaNetService_AlgDns.description:
Grouping for DNS ALG configuration. Defines DNS packet inspection
and filtering options for Distributed Services Switches (DSS).

dns-alg.description:
Domain Name System (DNS) ALG configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of DNS packets
with options to drop anomalous packets and limit message size.

drop-large-domain-name-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where any label length
is 64 bytes or higher, exceeding the DNS specification limit.
Default: false.

drop-long-label-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where the total domain
name size exceeds 255 bytes. Default: false.

drop-multi-question-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets that contain more than
one question in the query section. This helps prevent
certain DNS-based attacks. Default: false.

max-message-length.description:
Maximum allowed DNS message length in bytes. Messages
exceeding this length are dropped. Valid range: 1-8129.
Default: 512 bytes.

dns-alg.description:
Domain Name System (DNS) ALG configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of DNS packets
with options to drop anomalous packets and limit message size.

drop-large-domain-name-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where any label length
is 64 bytes or higher, exceeding the DNS specification limit.
Default: false.

drop-long-label-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where the total domain
name size exceeds 255 bytes. Default: false.

drop-multi-question-packets.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets that contain more than
one question in the query section. This helps prevent
certain DNS-based attacks. Default: false.

max-message-length.description:
Maximum allowed DNS message length in bytes. Messages
exceeding this length are dropped. Valid range: 1-8129.
Default: 512 bytes.

ArubaNetService_AlgFtp.description:
Grouping for FTP ALG configuration. Defines FTP packet inspection
options for Distributed Services Switches (DSS).

ftp-alg.description:
File Transfer Protocol (FTP) ALG configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of FTP control
connections to correctly handle dynamic data port negotiation.
The net-service protocol must be TCP (protocol 6 or IP_TCP).

allow-mismatch-ip-address.description:
When set to true, allows FTP data connections where the IP
address in the FTP PORT/PASV command payload differs from
the IP header source address. This is useful in NAT
environments. Default: false.

ArubaNetService_AlgIcmp.description:
Grouping for ICMP ALG configuration. Defines ICMP type and code
filters for Distributed Services Switches (DSS).

icmp-alg.description:
Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) ALG configuration
for Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Allows filtering
ICMP traffic by specific message type and code.

code.description:
ICMP code that provides additional detail for the specified
ICMP type. This is a required field. For example, for type 3
(Destination Unreachable), code 0 means Network Unreachable
and code 1 means Host Unreachable. Valid range: 0-18.

type.description:
ICMP message type number. This is a required field. Common
values include 0 (Echo Reply), 3 (Destination Unreachable),
8 (Echo Request), and 11 (Time Exceeded). Valid range: 0-255.

ArubaNetService_AlgMsrpc.description:
Grouping for Microsoft RPC ALG configuration. Defines MSRPC program
UUIDs and timeout for Distributed Services Switches (DSS).

msrpc-alg.description:
Microsoft Remote Procedure Call (MSRPC) ALG configuration for
Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of
MSRPC endpoint mapper traffic to correctly handle dynamic
port assignments. The net-service protocol must be TCP or UDP
and the port must be 135 (endpoint mapper).

program-uuids.description:
List of MSRPC program UUIDs to inspect. Each UUID identifies
a specific MSRPC service interface.

items.description:
List of MSRPC program UUIDs to inspect. Each UUID identifies
a specific MSRPC service interface.
items.x-typeDescription:
A Universally Unique IDentifier in the string representation
defined in RFC 4122.  The canonical representation uses
lowercase characters.

The following is an example of a UUID in string representation:
f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6

timeout.description:
Timeout in seconds for tracking MSRPC endpoint bindings.
After this period, dynamically learned port mappings are
removed. Default: 60 seconds.

ArubaNetService_NetServicesSchemaGET.description:
Configuration container for network services. Net-services define
protocol and port combinations used to identify specific types of
network traffic in firewall policy rules. Each net-service can
specify a protocol (TCP, UDP, etc.), individual ports or port
ranges, and optional ALG processing for application-aware
traffic handling.

net-service.description:
List of network service definitions. Each net-service defines
a named protocol/port combination that can be referenced in
policy rules to match specific types of network traffic. The
key 'name' uniquely identifies the net-service.

alg-config.description:
Application Layer Gateway (ALG) configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). This container is only available when
alg-service is set to ICMP, DNS, FTP, MSRPC, or SUNRPC. Each
ALG type exposes its own sub-container with protocol-specific
configuration options.

alg-service.description:
Specifies the Application Layer Gateway (ALG) service type
for this net-service. ALG enables deep packet inspection
for application-specific protocols, allowing the firewall
to handle dynamic port negotiation and NAT traversal. The
selected ALG must be compatible with the configured protocol
(TCP, UDP, or other). See the must constraint for valid
protocol/ALG combinations.

x-enumDescriptions.DHCP:
Enables ALG for DHCP traffic allowing dynamic relay and
inspection of DHCP messages. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.DNS:
Enables ALG for DNS traffic allowing inspection and optional
filtering of DNS queries and responses. Requires UDP protocol.
Additional DNS ALG options can be configured via the alg-config
container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.FACETIME:
Enables ALG for Apple FaceTime video calling traffic.
Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.FTP:
Enables ALG for FTP traffic allowing inspection and NAT
traversal of FTP control and data connections. Requires TCP
protocol. Additional FTP ALG options can be configured via
the alg-config container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.H323:
Enables ALG for H.323 video conferencing and VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.ICMP:
Enables ALG for ICMP traffic allowing inspection by type
and code. Additional ICMP ALG options can be configured via
the alg-config container when this value is selected.
x-enumDescriptions.JABBER:
Enables ALG for Cisco Jabber unified communications traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.MSRPC:
Enables ALG for Microsoft RPC (Remote Procedure Call) traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol on port 135. Additional MSRPC
ALG options can be configured via the alg-config container.
x-enumDescriptions.NOE:
Enables ALG for Alcatel NOE (New Office Environment) VoIP
traffic. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.RTSP:
Enables ALG for RTSP (Real Time Streaming Protocol) media
streaming traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SCCP:
Enables ALG for SCCP (Skinny Client Control Protocol) used
by Cisco IP phones. Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SIP:
Enables ALG for SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP or UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SIPS:
Enables ALG for SIPS (SIP over TLS) encrypted VoIP
signaling traffic. Requires TCP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.SUNRPC:
Enables ALG for SUN RPC (Remote Procedure Call) traffic.
Requires TCP or UDP protocol on port 111. Additional SUNRPC
ALG options can be configured via the alg-config container.
x-enumDescriptions.SVP:
Enables ALG for SVP (SpectraLink Voice Priority) wireless
VoIP traffic. Requires a protocol other than TCP or UDP.
x-enumDescriptions.TFTP:
Enables ALG for TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol)
traffic. Requires UDP protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.VOCERA:
Enables ALG for Vocera badge communication traffic.
Requires UDP protocol.

alg-service.x-typeDescription:
Application Layer Gateway (ALG) service types. Each ALG type
enables deep packet inspection for a specific application protocol,
allowing the firewall to understand and correctly handle protocol-specific
behavior such as dynamic port negotiation and NAT traversal.

description.description:
An optional human-readable description for this net-service.
Can be used to document the purpose or intended use.
Maximum length is 128 characters.

http-proxy.description:
When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTP
proxy port for web traffic interception. Only applicable
when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

https-proxy.description:
When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTPS
proxy port for secure web traffic interception. Only
applicable when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

name.description:
Unique name of the net-service. This is a required key field.
Maximum length is 63 characters.

port-range.description:
Port range specification for this net-service. If operator
is COMPARISON_RANGE, both min and max values define the range.
If operator is COMPARISON_EQ, only the min value is used as
the exact port match. Cannot be used together with the ports
leaf-list.

max.description:
Upper bound of port range. Only applicable when operator
is COMPARISON_RANGE. Must be greater than min. Protocol
must be TCP or UDP.
max.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

min.description:
Port value or lower bound of port range. When operator
is COMPARISON_EQ, this is the exact port to match. When
operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, this is the lower bound.
Protocol must be TCP or UDP.
min.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

operator.description:
Comparison operator for port matching. When set to
COMPARISON_EQ, matches a single port (min). When set
to COMPARISON_RANGE, matches all ports between min
and max inclusive. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

x-enumDescriptions.COMPARISON_RANGE: Minimum and maximum values of range.

ports.description:
List of individual port numbers for this net-service. Cannot
be used together with port-range. The protocol must be TCP
or UDP when ports are specified.

items.description:
List of individual port numbers for this net-service. Cannot
be used together with port-range. The protocol must be TCP
or UDP when ports are specified.
items.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

protocol.description:
Specifies the IP protocol for this net-service, expressed
either as an IP protocol number or a named identity (e.g.,
IP_TCP for 6, IP_UDP for 17). This determines which transport
protocol the service matches. Must not be set when alg-service
is ICMP.

oneOf.x-typeDescription: IP Protocol types.

ArubaPolicyCondition_AggregateRulesInfo.description:
Metadata for policy rule aggregation by role. Groups multiple role-based rules together
for optimized evaluation and reporting. Used internally to track related rules.

aggregate-info.description:
Read-only aggregation metadata for role-based policy rules. Only applicable when the address
type is ADDRESS_ROLE. Contains information about related rules that have been grouped together
for efficient evaluation.

agg-roles.description:
List of roles that have been aggregated together in the policy evaluation. Each entry
includes the role name and its corresponding rule position for tracking purposes.

agg-role.description: Name of the user role that has been aggregated into this policy rule group. Maximum 256 characters.

agg-rule-pos.description:
Position of the rule within the aggregated group. Used to track the evaluation order
of rules within the same aggregation set.

ArubaPolicyCondition_AggregateRulesInfoG.description:
Metadata for policy rule aggregation by role. Groups multiple role-based rules together
for optimized evaluation and reporting. Used internally to track related rules.

aggregate-info.description:
Read-only aggregation metadata for role-based policy rules. Only applicable when the address
type is ADDRESS_ROLE. Contains information about related rules that have been grouped together
for efficient evaluation.

agg-roles.description:
List of roles that have been aggregated together in the policy evaluation. Each entry
includes the role name and its corresponding rule position for tracking purposes.

agg-role.description: Name of the user role that has been aggregated into this policy rule group. Maximum 256 characters.

agg-rule-pos.description:

of rules within the same aggregation set.

ArubaPolicyCondition_DestinationConfig.description:
Complete destination address matching configuration for policy rules. Defines all destination
address criteria including IP addresses, roles, groups, domain names, and aliases with optional
role-based refinements.

destination.description:
Destination address matching criteria for the policy rule. Specifies which destination IP
addresses, roles, domain names, or address groups the rule applies to. The match type is
determined by the type field.

address-group.description:
Reference to a pre-configured IPv4 or IPv6 address group object. Only applicable when type is
ADDRESS_GROUP. Address groups allow you to create reusable sets of destination IP addresses or subnets.
The address group must be created before it can be referenced in a policy.

domain-name.description:
Destination domain name (FQDN) for matching. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_DOMAIN_NAME.
Matches traffic destined to the specified fully qualified domain name. Uses DNS resolution to
match against the domain's IP addresses. Maximum 256 characters. For AP devices only.

host-address.description:
Destination host IP address matching. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_HOST. Specify either
an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or reference to a host alias. Only one addressing method can be
used at a time.

invert.description:
Inverts the destination match logic. When set to true, matches all destinations EXCEPT the
specified destination. For AP devices only. Defaults to false.

net-group.description:
Reference to a named network group (net-group) for destination address matching. Only applicable
when type is ADDRESS_ALIAS. Network groups allow you to create reusable sets of destination IP

network-address.description:

role.description:

role-list.description:

items.description:

subnet-address.description:

devices only. The network-subnet-address field is required.

network-subnet-address.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 prefix followed by a slash and a subnet mask.

oneOf.x-typeDescription: An IPv4 prefix represented in dotted quad notation followed by a slash and a subnet mask in dotted quad notation.
An IPv6 prefix represented in full, shortened, or mixed shortened format followed by a slash and another IPv6-formatted subnet mask. Must be a contiguous network mask.

type.description:

x-enumDescriptions.ADDRESS_SUBNET_MASK: IPv4 or IPv6 address with subnet mask.

Additional matching options for destination role-based policies. Allows combining role-based
matching with specific IP addresses or network prefixes to create more granular policies.

host-address.description:

host-address-alias.description:

net-group.description:

network-address.description:

ip-prefix-alias.description:

options-type.description:
