ArubaPolicyCondition_EthernetHeaderConfi.description:
Defines Layer 2 Ethernet frame matching criteria including MAC addresses, EtherType,
VLAN tags, and priority values. Used for MAC ACL rules and advanced Layer 2 filtering.

ethernet-header.description:
Layer 2 Ethernet frame matching criteria. Specifies MAC addresses, EtherType, VLAN identifiers,
and priority code points to match against. Used for MAC-based access control and Layer 2 filtering.

destination-mac.description:
Destination MAC address to match in Ethernet frames. Specified in IEEE 802 format (e.g.,
aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff). Use with destination-mac-mask for wildcard matching of MAC address ranges.

destination-mac-mask.description:
Wildcard mask for destination MAC address matching. Specified in IEEE 802 format. A zero bit
indicates the corresponding bit in the MAC address must match; a one bit indicates don't care.
Use this for matching ranges of MAC addresses.

ethermask.description:
Wildcard mask for EtherType matching. A zero bit indicates the corresponding bit in the
EtherType must match; a one bit indicates don't care. Use this for matching ranges of
EtherType values. For gateway devices only.

ethertype.description:
EtherType field value to match in Ethernet frames. Identifies the protocol encapsulated in
the payload (e.g., 0x0800 for IPv4, 0x86DD for IPv6, 0x0806 for ARP). Use with ethermask
for wildcard matching.

x-enumDescriptions.ETHERTYPE_VLAN:
VLAN-tagged frame (as defined by IEEE 802.1q) (0x8100). Note
that this value is also used to represent Shortest Path
Bridging (IEEE 801.1aq) frames.

oneOf.x-typeDescription: Ethernet Protocol types.

pcp.description:
IEEE 802.1Q Priority Code Point (PCP) value to match in tagged Ethernet frames. Specifies
the priority level for QoS (0=lowest, 7=highest). Only applicable for VLAN-tagged traffic.
For switch devices only. Valid range: 0-7.

source-mac.description:
Source MAC address to match in Ethernet frames. Specified in IEEE 802 format (e.g., aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff).
Use with source-mac-mask for wildcard matching of MAC address ranges.

source-mac-mask.description:
Wildcard mask for source MAC address matching. Specified in IEEE 802 format. A zero bit indicates
the corresponding bit in the MAC address must match; a one bit indicates don't care. Use this
for matching ranges of MAC addresses.

vlan.description:
VLAN identifier to match in IEEE 802.1Q tagged Ethernet frames. Use this to match traffic
on a specific VLAN. For switch devices only. Valid range: 0-4000.

ArubaPolicyCondition_IpProtocolFieldsCom.description:
Defines IP header matching criteria common to both IPv4 and IPv6. Includes protocol type,
DSCP, ToS, ECN, TTL/hop-limit, and protocol-specific fields for ICMP and IGMP.

ip-header.description:
IP header matching criteria. Specifies Layer 3 packet header fields to match including protocol,
quality of service markings (DSCP, ToS), hop limit (TTL), and protocol-specific parameters for
ICMP and IGMP.

dscp.description:
Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value to match in the IP header. Used for identifying
and classifying traffic based on QoS markings. Valid values are DSCP keywords (e.g., default, af11,
ef) or numeric values (0-63). Cannot be used simultaneously with IP Precedence or ToS fields.

x-enumDescriptions.AF11: DSCP 10 (Assured Forwarding class 1, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF12: DSCP 12 (Assured Forwarding class 1, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF13: DSCP 14 (Assured Forwarding class 1, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF21: DSCP 18 (Assured Forwarding class 2, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF22: DSCP 20 (Assured Forwarding class 2, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF23: DSCP 22 (Assured Forwarding class 2, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF31: DSCP 26 (Assured Forwarding class 3, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF32: DSCP 28 (Assured Forwarding class 3, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF33: DSCP 30 (Assured Forwarding class 3, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF41: DSCP 34 (Assured Forwarding class 4, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF42: DSCP 36 (Assured Forwarding class 4, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF43: DSCP 38 (Assured Forwarding class 4, high drop probability)

oneOf.x-typeDescription: DSCP value enum types

ecn.description:
Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) bits to match in the IP header. Used to signal network
congestion without dropping packets. Cannot be used simultaneously with IP Precedence or ToS fields.
ecn.x-typeDescription: Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) marking in the IP header.

fragment.description:
Match IP packets with the fragmentation flag set or that are fragmented. When set to true,
matches fragmented packets only. For CX switches only. Used to identify and handle packet
fragmentation scenarios.

hop-limit.description:
Hop limit to match in IP packets. Known as TTL (Time To Live) in IPv4 packets and hop limit in
IPv6 packets. Specifies the maximum number of hops (router traversals) a packet can make before
being discarded. Valid range: 0-255.

icmp.description:
ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) matching criteria. Only applicable when the protocol
is ICMP (1) or ICMPv6 (58). Specifies ICMP message type and code to match against (e.g., echo
request, destination unreachable).

icmp-code.description:
ICMP message code as a numeric value. Provides additional specificity for the ICMP type
(e.g., for type 3 destination-unreachable: code 0=network-unreachable, code 1=host-unreachable).
Used in conjunction with icmp-type. Valid range: 0-255.

icmp-enum.description:
ICMP message type using predefined enumeration values (e.g., echo-request, echo-reply,
destination-unreachable). Provides a user-friendly way to specify common ICMP types.

icmp-type.description:
ICMP message type as a numeric value (e.g., 0=echo-reply, 3=destination-unreachable, 8=echo-request).
Use with icmp-code to match specific ICMP messages. Valid range: 0-255.

igmp.description:
IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) matching criteria. Only applicable when the protocol
is IGMP. Specifies IGMP message type to match against (e.g., membership query, membership report).

type.description:
IGMP message type using predefined enumeration values (e.g., membership-query, membership-report,
leave-group). Used to match specific IGMP protocol messages for multicast group management.

ip-precedence.description:
IP Precedence value to match in the IP ToS field. Legacy QoS field used for traffic priority.
Valid range: 0-7 (0=routine, 7=network control). Cannot be used simultaneously with DSCP or ECN
fields. For switch devices only.

ipv6-fragmentation-header.description:
IPv6 fragmentation header value to match. Used to identify fragmented IPv6 packets. Only
applicable for IPv6 traffic.

protocol.description:
IP protocol to match in the packet. Can be specified either as a protocol number (e.g., 6 for TCP,
17 for UDP, 1 for ICMP) or by a named protocol identifier (e.g., IP_TCP, IP_UDP, IP_ICMP). This
determines which transport protocol the rule applies to.

oneOf.x-typeDescription: IP Protocol types.

tos.description:
Type of Service (ToS) value to match in the IP header. Legacy QoS field used for traffic
classification. Valid range: 0-63. Cannot be used simultaneously with DSCP or ECN fields.
For switch devices only.

vlan.description:
VLAN identifier to match in IP packets. Matches traffic on the specified VLAN. Valid range:
1-4094. For switch devices only. Use this to apply policies to traffic on specific VLANs.

ArubaPolicyCondition_PortConfig.description:
Port matching criteria with comparison operator. Specifies how to match against port numbers:
single port (equals), port range (minimum and maximum), or port comparison (less than,
greater than). When operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, both min and max values are required;
otherwise only the min value is used.

group.description:
Reference to a pre-configured port group object. Only applicable when operator is PORT_GROUP.
The port group allows you to match against multiple ports or port ranges defined in a single
reusable object. The port group must be created before it can be referenced in a policy.

max.description:
Upper bound of port range. Only applicable when operator is COMPARISON_RANGE. Must be
greater than or equal to the min value. Valid range: 0-65535.
max.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

min.description:
Port number to match, or the lower bound of a port range when operator is COMPARISON_RANGE.
For single port matching, this is the exact port number. Valid range: 0-65535.
min.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

operator.description:
Comparison operator for port matching. Specifies how to compare the packet's port number
against the configured value: equals, not equals, less than, greater than, range, or
reference to a port group object.

x-enumDescriptions.COMPARISON_RANGE: Minimum and maximum values of range.

ArubaPolicyCondition_PortConfigGet.description:
Port matching criteria with comparison operator. Specifies how to match against port numbers:
single port (equals), port range (minimum and maximum), or port comparison (less than,

ArubaPolicyCondition_SourceBaseConfig.description:
Defines source address matching criteria for policy rules. Supports various address types
including individual hosts, networks, address groups, roles, and aliases.

address-group.description:
Reference to a pre-configured IPv4 or IPv6 address group object. Only applicable when type
is ADDRESS_GROUP. Address groups allow you to create reusable sets of IP addresses or subnets.
The address group must be created before it can be referenced in a policy.

host-address.description:
Source host IP address matching. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_HOST. Specify either
an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or reference to a host alias. Only one addressing method
can be used at a time.

network-address.description:
Source network IP prefix matching using CIDR notation. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_NETWORK.
Specify either an IPv4 prefix (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8), IPv6 prefix (e.g., 2001:db8::/32), or reference
to a network alias. Only one addressing method can be used at a time.

subnet-address.description:
Source network address with subnet mask notation. Only applicable when type is ADDRESS_SUBNET_MASK.
Specify an IPv4 or IPv6 network with a subnet mask (e.g., 192.168.1.0/255.255.255.0). For
switch devices only. The network-subnet-address field is required.

network-subnet-address.description:

ArubaPolicyCondition_TransportFieldsConf.description:
Defines transport-layer (Layer 4) matching criteria including source and destination ports,
TCP flags, and connection state. Applicable for TCP, UDP, and SCTP protocols.

transport-fields.description:
Transport-layer (Layer 4) packet matching criteria. Specifies source and destination ports,
TCP flags, and connection state to match against. Only applicable for TCP, UDP, and SCTP protocols.

destination-port.description:
Destination port number or range to match. Only applicable when the protocol is TCP (6),
UDP (17), or SCTP (132). Use this to match traffic destined to specific services or applications.

destination-port-net-group.description:
Reference to a named network service for destination port matching. The network service defines
a reusable set of ports and protocols for matching traffic destined to specific services.

established.description:
Match packets belonging to an established TCP connection. Only applicable for TCP traffic.
When set to true, matches TCP packets with ACK or RST flags set, indicating the connection
is already established. Useful for stateful firewall rules to allow return traffic.
Cannot be used simultaneously with both TCP_RST and TCP_ACK flags. Defaults to false.

source-port.description:
Source port number or range to match. Only applicable when the protocol is TCP (6), UDP (17),
or SCTP (132). Use this to match traffic originating from specific ports.

source-port-net-group.description:
Reference to a named network service for source port matching. The network service defines
a reusable set of ports and protocols for matching traffic originating from specific services.

tcp-flags.description:
List of TCP control flags to match (e.g., SYN, ACK, FIN, RST). Only applicable for TCP traffic.
Use this to match specific TCP connection states or control packets. Multiple flags can be specified.

items.description:
List of TCP control flags to match (e.g., SYN, ACK, FIN, RST). Only applicable for TCP traffic.
Use this to match specific TCP connection states or control packets. Multiple flags can be specified.

x-enumDescriptions.TCP_ECE:
TCP ECN-Echo flag.  If the SYN flag is set, indicates that
the TCP peer is ECN-capable, otherwise indicates that a
packet with Congestion Experienced flag in the IP header
is set

ArubaDhcpPool_DhcpPoolSchemaGET.description:
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) pool profiles automate IP
address assignment and network configuration delivery to client
devices joining the network. DHCP servers use pools to manage
IPv4/IPv6 address ranges, DNS settings, gateway information, lease
durations, and vendor-specific options (DHCP Options 43, 60, etc.).
This module supports DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 with static bindings, DDNS
integration, and network boot configuration. Requires DDNS profiles
for dynamic DNS updates. Device Limits: Gateway supports up to 256
DHCPv4 static reservations, 1 IP address per DHCPv4 option code. Use
this API to retrieve the list of DHCP pool profiles.

profile.description:
DHCP pool profile defining address ranges, lease times, DNS servers,
gateway addresses, domain names, and vendor options for DHCPv4 or
DHCPv6. Each entity is identified by profile name. Use these APIs
to create, modify, or delete a DHCP pool profile instance.

domain.description: Domain Name
domain.x-typeDescription:
The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

ArubaDhcpRelay_DhcpRelaySchemaGET.description:
DHCP Relay forwards DHCP requests from clients on one network
segment to DHCP servers located on different network
segments, enabling centralized IP address management across
multiple subnets. DHCP Relay supports DHCPv4 (RFC 2131) and
DHCPv6 (RFC 3315) with configurable helper addresses, Option
82 insertion for client identification, hop count control,
and smart relay functionality. Configure IPv4 and IPv6 relay
parameters including server addresses, source interfaces, and
DHCP option handling policies. Use this API to retrieve the
list of DHCP relay profiles.

profile.description:
DHCP relay profile defining DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 relay agent parameters
including server addresses, Option 82 handling, hop count settings,
and source interface selection. Each entity is identified by profile
name. Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete a DHCP relay
profile instance.

enable.description:
Enables DHCPv4 relay globally. The functionality is effective
  	 only after the port level helper configuration.

hop-count-increment.description: Enables hop count increment in the relayed DHCPv4 requests.

l2vpn-clients.description: Enables DHCPv4 relay for remote L2 VPN clients.

option-xml.description:
IPv4 DHCP relay option XML file. The XML file is used as the input from the user and is validated
against an XSD file in the controller. The format in the XML file is parsed and stored in the DHCP
relay which is used to insert Option-82 related values in the DHCP request packets sent from the
client to the server.

reply-overwrite-source-ip.description: Enables DHCPv4 relay overwrite source IP.

smart-relay.description:
Enables DHCPv4 smart relay globally. When multiple IPv4 addresses are configured on an
interface, the primary IP address is used first as the gateway IP (GIADDR) for DHCP relay.
If the DHCP server does not have available IP addresses in the pool corresponding to the primary
IP's subnet, the secondary IP address is used as a fallback. This ensures that the DHCP relay
remains functional by switching to a secondary IP address when the primary IP's subnet pool
is exhausted.

ArubaExternalStorage_ExternalStorageSche.description:
External storage volumes accessible from the switch.
The feature manages external storage volumes and make them
available to system applications and protocols.
The storage is used to store and retrieve data files when
capacity use pattern is such that external storage is the
best choice. The feature supports network attached storage
as well as local external storage.

profile.description: Global profile for External storage and External storage parameters.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

ArubaIpLockdown_IpSourceLockdownSchemaGE.description:
IP source lockdown.
IP source lockdown feature is used to prevent IP source address
spoofing on a per-port basis. When dynamic IP source lockdown is
enabled, IP traffic received on a port are forwarded only if IP
address, VLAN, MAC address and Port matches the IP binding entry. The
IP binding can either be statically configured or learnt by the DHCP
Snooping feature.

WAN SLA profile intended for Gateway and Microbranch AP platforms.

Creates an IPSLA profile (when sla-destination is set to
SLA_DESTINATION_MANUAL or SLA_DESTINATION_TUNNEL) that can be attached
to a Nexthop for Policy Based Routing(PBR) or a Threshold profile
(when sla-destination is set to SLA_THRESHOLD_WAN_HEALTH_CHECK)
that can be attached to a DPS WAN policy for steering the traffic
over the compliant uplink/tunnel or a SaaS Threshold profile (when
sla-destination is set to SLA_THRESHOLD_WAN_HEALTH_CHECK and the
profile is configured as saas-threshold-profile) that can be attached
to a SaaS Express application to forward the application traffic over
the best performing uplink.

start-value.x-typeDescription:
A date and time, expressed in the format described in RFC3339.
That is to say:

YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ+-hh:mm

where YYYY is the year, MM is the month expressed as a two-digit
month (zero padding if required), DD is the day of the month,
expressed as a two digit value. T is the literal character 'T',
HH is the hour of the day expressed as a two digit number, using
the 24-hour clock, MM is the minute of the hour expressed as a
two digit number. Z is the literal character 'Z', followed by a
timezone offset expressed in hours (hh) and minutes (mm), both
expressed as two digit numbers. The time offset is specified as
a positive or negative offset to UTC using the '+' or '-'
character preceding the offset.

Optionally, fractional seconds can be expressed after the minute
of the hour as a decimal number of unspecified precision
reflecting fractions of a second.

stop.description: Schedule type to stop the session.

x-enumDescriptions.FOREVER: Schedule to run the IP SLA forever.
x-enumDescriptions.REPEAT: Number of times the IP SLA tests to be repeated.
x-enumDescriptions.STOP_TIME: Stop time for the IPSLA session.

ArubaMgmd_MgmdGlobalSchemaGET.description:
Multicast Group Membership Discovery (MGMD) manages multicast
group membership using IGMP (Internet Group Management
Protocol) for IPv4 and MLD (Multicast Listener Discovery) for
IPv6 networks. MGMD enables efficient multicast traffic
delivery by controlling group membership, reducing unnecessary
flooding, and conserving network bandwidth. Configure IGMP
snooping, MLD snooping, querier functionality, fast-leave
processing, static groups, proxy domains, and query intervals
for multicast optimization. Use this API to retrieve the list
of MGMD profiles.

profile.description:
MGMD profile defining IGMP and MLD snooping parameters, querier
settings, fast-leave options, static multicast groups, and refresh
intervals for multicast traffic management. Each entity is
identified by profile name. Use these APIs to create, modify, or
delete an MGMD profile instance.

enable.description:
Enable global IGMP for MGMD.
IGMP is used as a communication protocol by the hosts and adjacent routers
to deliver multicast service with IPv4 networks.

Enable global MLD for MGMD.
MLD is used as a communication protocol by the hosts and adjacent routers
to deliver multicast service with IPv6 networks.

refresh-client.description:

periodically.

ArubaMulticastDns_MdnsSdProfileCfg.description: Configure multicast DNS Service Discovery Profile rules

filter-rule.description:
Configure filter rules associated with the service profile.
The sequence number configured determines the priority with which the rule is
matched. Lower the sequence number, higher is the priority. Filter match parameters
include service-name and service-instance-name. When no match criteria is specified
in the rule, then the rule can be matched against any mDNS packet. Once the match is
found then either the packet can be permitted or denied based on the action specified
in the rule.

instance-name.description: Match parameter mDNS SD service instance name

match-service-group.description: Match parameter mDNS SD service group

ArubaNdSnooping_NdSnoopingSchemaGET.description:
Configuration of ND-Snooping.
Enabling the ND-Snooping feature on your switches prevents
ND attacks. ND-Snooping does not just snoop but also detect
attacks by default. ND-Snooping drops invalid ND packets
and, together with DIPLDv6, blocks data traffic from invalid hosts.

ArubaQosGlobal_QSchedProfileConfig.description: Combined QoS queue- and schedule-profile global pairing.

q-profile.description:
Queue profile to apply in combination with the specified
schedule profile. Queue profiles must first be configured using the
aruba-qos-queue yang model, and must be valid for the platform to
which the profile is being applied.

Queue profiles cannot be modified while they are applied. The number
of queues and queue ID values must also match those in the paired
schedule profile. If an applied queue profile is modified, the
configuration will be rejected. To apply the modified queue profile,
follow the following sequence of operations:

1. If sched-profile in aruba-qos-global is set to DEFAULT, set
q-profile to DEFAULT. Otherwise, remove both q-profile and
sched-profile. This will cause the factory-default profiles
to be applied.
2. For PVOS devices, ensure that the traffic-template leaf is not
set to the same profile as the queue-profile being modified. If it
is, delete the traffic-template by setting the traffic-template
leaf to null.
3. Modify the queue profile.
4. If both q-profile and sched-profile were removed in step 1,
apply them again together in the same transaction. If q-profile
was set to DEFAULT in step 1, apply only the queue profile.
5. For PVOS devices, if the traffic template was removed as part of
this process, apply it again after the queue profile
has been modified.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
The QoS factory-default profile definition. This can be
used to apply default Queue and/or Schedule profiles.

sched-profile.description:
Schedule profile to apply in combination with the specified
queue profile. Schedule profiles must first be configured using the
aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be valid for the platform to
which the profile is being applied. The number of queues and queue ID
values must also match those in the paired queue profile.

Name or description of the entity. Must be 1-64 characters in length and can only
contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

profile.description:
QoS Queue Profile. This profile is used to assign priorities to
queues, to determine servicing. Once it has been created, a queue
profile can be globally applied in combination with a separately-
created schedule profile, using the aruba-qos-global yang model. The
queue and schedule profiles must be valid for the platform to which
they are being applied, and the configured number of queues and the
queue ID values must match.

Platform-dependent queue profile restrictions may include requiring
profiles to start with queue zero and requiring all queues in the
profiles to be adjacent.

AOSCX: All local priorities must be mapped to a queue, with no
duplicates.
PVOS: Profiles can only be configured for 2, 4, or 8 queues. All cos
values must be mapped to a queue, with no duplicates.

Queue profiles cannot be modified while they are applied. If an
applied queue profile is modified, the configuration is rejected.
To apply the modified queue profile, follow the following sequence
of operations:

1. If sched-profile in aruba-qos-global is set to DEFAULT, set
  q-profile to DEFAULT. Otherwise, remove both q-profile and
  sched-profile. This will cause the factory-default profiles
  to be applied.
2. For PVOS devices, ensure that the traffic-template leaf in
  aruba-qos-global is not set to the same profile as the
  queue-profile being modified. If it is, delete the
  aruba-qos-global traffic-template by setting the traffic-template
  leaf to null.
3. Modify the queue profile.
4. If both q-profile and sched-profile were removed in step 1, apply
  them again together in the same transaction. If q-profile was set
  to DEFAULT in step 1, apply only the q-profile leaf in aruba-qos-global.
5. If the traffic-template leaf in aruba-qos-global was set to null
  as part of this process, apply it again after the queue profile
  has been modified.

profile.description:
QoS Schedule Profile. These profiles are used to determine bandwidth
allocation for the queues and how they will be serviced. They can
include minimum-bandwidths, weighted queues, all-strict queues,
weighted plus a strict top queue, or minimum-bandwidths plus a strict
top queue.

'Strict' priority will service all packets in a queue before any
packets in lower-numbered queues, as long as there are no packets in
any higher-numbered queues.

'Weighted' queuing will apportion available bandwidth among all non-
empty weighted queues in relation to their queue weights.

'Min_bandwidth' queuing will apportion available bandwidth among all
non-empty min-bandwidth queues in relation to their configured
percentages.

Once it has been created, a schedule profile can be globally applied
in combination with a separately-created queue profile, using the
aruba-qos-global yang model. The queue and schedule profiles must be
valid for the platform to which they are being applied, and the
configured number of queues and the queue ID values must match. Valid
schedule profiles can also be applied to ports, using the
aruba-interface-ethernet and/or aruba-interface-portchannel yang models.

ArubaUdpBroadcastForwarder_UdpBroadcastF.description:
Configure UDP Broadcast Forwarder globally.
The routers by default do not forward broadcast packets.
However, there are situations where it is desirable to
forward certain broadcast packets. The UDP (User Datagram
Protocol) broadcast forwarder takes the client's UDP
broadcast packets and forwards to the configured server(s)
in a different subnet. UDP broadcast forwarding is
supported only for IPv4 addresses.

contracts with WebCC content categories and a traffic direction, enabling
rate limiting based on the type of web content being accessed

There can be at most one contract per category per direction.

web-reputation-aaa-contract.description:
WebCC reputation-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA bandwidth
contracts with WebCC reputation risk levels and a traffic direction, enabling
differentiated rate limiting based on the trustworthiness of web destinations.
Risk levels are: TRUSTWORTHY (81-100), LOW_RISK (61-80), MODERATE_RISK (41-60),
SUSPICIOUS (21-40), and HIGH_RISK (1-20).

web-reputation.description:

risk level and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC reputation
level (TRUSTWORTHY, LOW_RISK, MODERATE_RISK, SUSPICIOUS, or HIGH_RISK)
to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream
traffic. There can be at most one contract per risk level per direction.

ArubaPolicyCondition_ServiceConfig.description:
Defines application-aware and network service matching criteria for policy rules,
including applications, application categories, web categories, web reputation,
and named network services.

services.description:
Application-aware and network service matching criteria. Specifies which
applications, web categories, or network services the policy rule applies to.

app-category.description:
Application category to match (e.g., collaboration, file-sharing, messaging). Only
applicable when the rule type is RULE_APP_CATEGORY. Matches all applications belonging
to the specified category.

application.description:
Specific application to match (e.g., Zoom, Dropbox, Netflix). Only applicable when
the rule type is RULE_APPLICATION. Uses deep packet inspection (DPI) to identify
the application regardless of port or protocol.

apptag-name.description:
Aruba application tag name for application visibility and control. Only applicable when
the rule type is RULE_APPTAG. Must be used in conjunction with apptag-type. Identifies
an application discovered through Aruba's application classification.

apptag-type.description:
Aruba application tag type classification. Only applicable when the rule type is RULE_APPTAG.
Must be used in conjunction with apptag-name. Categorizes the application for visibility
and policy enforcement.

net-service.description:
Named network service to match. Only applicable when the rule type is RULE_NET_SERVICE.
References a pre-configured network service that defines protocol, ports, and other
transport-layer parameters.

web-category.description:
Web content category to match (e.g., social-media, gaming, streaming). Only applicable
when the rule type is RULE_WEB_CATEGORY or RULE_WEB_CAT_REP. Used for URL filtering.

web-reputation.description:
Web reputation score to match (e.g., trustworthy, suspicious, malicious). Only applicable
when the rule type is RULE_WEB_REPUTATION or RULE_WEB_CAT_REP. Used for threat prevention.

x-enumDescriptions.HIGH_RISK: Reputation score of 1-20 is deemed high-risk.
x-enumDescriptions.LOW_RISK: Reputation score of 61-80 is deemed low-risk.
x-enumDescriptions.MODERATE_RISK: Reputation score of 41-60 is deemed moderate-risk.
x-enumDescriptions.SUSPICIOUS: Reputation score of 21-40 is deemed suspicious.
x-enumDescriptions.TRUSTWORTHY: Reputation score of 81-100 is deemed Trustworthy.

web-reputation.x-typeDescription: WebCC URL reputation score ranges that determine risk level.

ArubaPolicyGroup_PolicyGrouping.description: Defines the ordered list of firewall policies and their global evaluation sequence.

policy-group-list.description:
An ordered list of firewall policies with their evaluation priorities.
Policies are evaluated in ascending order by position (lower values first).
Each policy name must be unique, and each position must be unique within the group.

description.description:
A user-defined description explaining the purpose or context of this policy's
placement in the evaluation sequence. Maximum length is 256 characters.

name.description:
Unique identifier for the firewall policy. This name must reference an existing
policy configured in the system. Maximum length is 256 characters.

position.description:
The evaluation priority of this policy in the global policy sequence. Policies are
evaluated in ascending order (lower numbers are evaluated first). This value must be
unique across all policies in the group. Valid range: 1 to 2000.

ArubaPolicy_ActionConfig.description:
Grouping for the action associated with a policy rule. Defines
the forwarding action (permit, deny, redirect, NAT, route, etc.)
and optional secondary actions (QoS, logging, mirroring, etc.).

action.description:
Specifies the action to take when traffic matches the rule
condition. Exactly one primary forwarding action type must be
configured. Secondary actions (logging, QoS, mirroring) can
be combined with the primary action.

secondary-actions.description:
Container for secondary actions that can be applied alongside
the primary forwarding action. Includes QoS settings (DSCP,
dot1p, rate-limit), logging, mirroring, denylist, bandwidth
throttling, and packet counting.

append-mirror-session.description:
Additional mirror session numbers to copy matched traffic
to. Up to 3 sessions can be appended. For PVOS switches only.

items.description:
Additional mirror session numbers to copy matched traffic
to. Up to 3 sessions can be appended. For PVOS switches only.
items.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a Mirror session

cos.description:
Sets the Layer 2 802.1Q Class of Service (CoS) value
(0-7) on matched packets. For CX switches only.

count.description:
When set to true, enables counting of packets matching
this rule for monitoring purposes. Default: false.

denylist.description:
When set to true, adds the source of matching traffic
to the deny list (formerly blacklist). Default: false.

disable-scanning.description:
When set to true, disables application scanning for
matched traffic on AP devices. Default: false.

dot1p-priority.description:
Sets the Layer 2 802.1Q Priority Code Point (PCP) value
(0-7) on matched packets for QoS prioritization.

dscp.description:
Sets the Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value
on matched packets for QoS classification. Not applicable
when the action type is ACTION_PACKET_MARKING.

x-enumDescriptions.AF11: DSCP 10 (Assured Forwarding class 1, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF12: DSCP 12 (Assured Forwarding class 1, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF13: DSCP 14 (Assured Forwarding class 1, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF21: DSCP 18 (Assured Forwarding class 2, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF22: DSCP 20 (Assured Forwarding class 2, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF23: DSCP 22 (Assured Forwarding class 2, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF31: DSCP 26 (Assured Forwarding class 3, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF32: DSCP 28 (Assured Forwarding class 3, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF33: DSCP 30 (Assured Forwarding class 3, high drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF41: DSCP 34 (Assured Forwarding class 4, low drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF42: DSCP 36 (Assured Forwarding class 4, medium drop probability)
x-enumDescriptions.AF43: DSCP 38 (Assured Forwarding class 4, high drop probability)

oneOf.x-typeDescription: DSCP value enum types

ip-precedence.description:
Sets the IP precedence value (0-7) on matched packets.
Not applicable when the action type is ACTION_PACKET_MARKING.

local-queue-priority.description:
Sets the local queue priority for matched traffic.
Can be a numeric value (0-7) or a named queue type.

oneOf.x-typeDescription: Queue type.

log.description:
When set to true, enables logging of traffic matching
this rule. Default: false.

markapp.description:
Tags matched traffic with a custom application identifier
for prioritization. For AP devices only.

x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM1: Selects the first custom application profile.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM2: Selects the second custom application profile.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM3: Selects the third custom application profile.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM4: Selects the fourth custom application profile.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOM5: Selects the fifth custom application profile.

markapp.x-typeDescription:
Enumeration of custom application profiles that can be
assigned to policy rules for application-level marking
on access point devices.

mirror.description:
When set to true, mirrors matched traffic for analysis
or troubleshooting. For AP and GW devices. Default: false.

mirror-session.description:
Specifies the mirror session number to copy matched traffic
to for switch devices (CX/PVOS).
mirror-session.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a Mirror session

rate-limit.description:
Rate limit for matched traffic in kilobytes per second.
Traffic exceeding this rate is dropped. Valid range:
1 to 4294967295 kb/sec.

throttle-downstream.description:
Maximum downstream bandwidth in kilobytes per second for
matched traffic. Applies throttling from network to client.
For AP devices only. Valid range: 1 to 4294966 kbytes/sec.

throttle-upstream.description:
Maximum upstream bandwidth in kilobytes per second for
matched traffic. Applies throttling from client to network.
For AP devices only. Valid range: 1 to 4294966 kbytes/sec.

vxlan-encap.description:
When set to true, enables VXLAN encapsulation for matched
traffic. Default: false.

send-deny-response.description:
When set to true, sends a TCP RST or ICMP unreachable response
to the client when traffic is denied, instead of silently
dropping the packet. Only applicable when action type is
ACTION_DENY. Default: false.

type.description:
Specifies the primary forwarding action for this rule.
ACTION_ALLOW permits the traffic. ACTION_DENY drops the
traffic. ACTION_REDIRECT redirects to a configured destination.
ACTION_SOURCE_NAT/ACTION_DESTINATION_NAT/ACTION_DUAL_NAT apply
NAT translations. ACTION_ROUTE uses policy-based routing.
ACTION_QOS applies QoS marking. Exactly one action type must
be specified per rule.

x-enumDescriptions.ACTION_FORWARD_IPSEC_VPNC: Forward to IPSEC map to VPNC.

ArubaPolicy_ConditionConfig.description:
Grouping for the triggering condition of a policy rule. Defines
the match criteria including rule type, address family, source,
destination, protocol, transport fields, and service parameters.

condition.description:
Specifies the match condition for a policy rule. The condition
determines which traffic the rule applies to based on criteria
such as protocol, source/destination addresses, ports, and
application or service identifiers.

address-family.description:
IP address family for the policy rule. Specifies whether
the rule applies to IPv4 or IPv6 traffic.

x-enumDescriptions.IPV4: IPv4 address family
x-enumDescriptions.IPV6: IPv6 address family

rule-type.description:
Specifies the rule type that determines what kind of traffic
matching is performed. RULE_ANY matches all traffic.

ArubaPolicy_PoliciesSchemaGET.description:
Policies define ordered sets of rules that match network
traffic and apply permit, deny, or advanced actions such as
NAT, redirect, and policy-based routing.

policy.description:
A firewall policy identified by a unique name. Each policy
contains an ordered set of rules that match traffic and
apply actions. ACL-type rules (RULE_ACL_IP, RULE_ACL_IPV6,
RULE_ACL_MAC) are only permitted in POLICY_NETWORK_ACL
policies.

association.description:
Specifies how this policy is associated with clients or
interfaces. Defaults to ASSOCIATION_ROLE (role-based
policy assignment).

description.description:
A user-defined description or comment for this policy.
Maximum 256 characters.

dsf-enable.description:
Enable distributed services firewall (DSF) for this policy.
When enabled, the policy type must be POLICY_TYPE_SECURITY.
Applicable to AOS-CX switches only. Defaults to false.

name.description:
Unique name of the policy. This is a required key field.
Maximum 145 characters. On AOS-CX, space (' ') and
question mark ('?') characters are not supported in
policy names.

type.description:
Type of policy. Determines the rule structure and actions
available. If dsf-enable is true, the type must be
POLICY_TYPE_SECURITY.

ArubaPolicy_PolicingActionGroup.description:
Grouping for QoS traffic policing policy actions. Supports
single-rate and two-rate three-color marker (trTCM) policing
to rate-limit traffic matching policy rules.

policing.description:
QoS traffic policing configuration for this policy rule.
Enforces rate limits on matching traffic using committed
information rate (CIR) and optional peak information rate
(PIR) parameters with configurable exceed actions.

committed-burst-size.description:
Committed Burst Size (CBS) in bytes. Maximum burst of
traffic allowed at the committed information rate before
packets are considered to exceed the rate.

committed-info-rate.description:
Committed Information Rate (CIR) in Kbps. Defines the
guaranteed bandwidth for matching traffic. Must be less
than the peak-info-rate (PIR) when two-rate policing
is configured.

exceed-action.description:
Action to take when traffic exceeds the configured rate.
For single-rate policing, this applies when CIR is
exceeded. For two-rate policing (POLICING_TR_TCM), this
applies when PIR is exceeded.

exceed-cir-dscp.description:
DSCP value to remark on packets that exceed the CIR but
are within the PIR. Only applicable when policing type is
POLICING_TR_TCM.

ArubaPolicy_PolicyRulesGroup.description:
Grouping for policy rules. Contains the ordered list of rules
that define the match conditions and actions for a policy.

policy-rule.description:
Ordered list of policy rules. Each rule defines a match
condition and action pair. Rules are evaluated in ascending
order by position (low to high). The key 'position' uniquely
identifies each rule within the policy.

description.description:
A user-defined description or comment for this policy rule.
Maximum length is 256 characters.

devices-applicable.description:
Read-only field indicating whether the rule is supported by
all or a subset of target devices. Values are 'full' (all
devices support this rule) or 'partial' (only some devices
support it).

position.description:
Sequence position that determines the order in which rules
are evaluated. This is a required key field. Lower values
are evaluated first. The position must be unique for each
rule within the policy.

ArubaPolicy_RedirectConfig.description:
Grouping for policy redirect configuration. Specifies the
redirection destination when the action type is ACTION_REDIRECT.

redirect.description:
Redirect configuration. Specifies where matched traffic
should be redirected to, such as a tunnel, tunnel-group,
or ESI (External Service Interface) group.

destination.description:
Specifies the redirect destination type. REDIRECT_TUNNEL
redirects to a specific GRE tunnel. REDIRECT_TUNNEL_GROUP
redirects to a tunnel group for load balancing. REDIRECT_ESI
redirects to an External Service Interface group.

x-enumDescriptions.REDIRECT_SLB: Redirect to Service Load Balancing (SLB) Group.

esi-direction.description:
Direction of ESI redirect (forward or reverse). Only
applicable when destination is REDIRECT_ESI.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Both directions.

esi-group.description:
ESI (External Service Interface) group name for redirect.
Only applicable when destination is REDIRECT_ESI. References
a configured SLB group.

tunnel.description:
Tunnel ID for redirect. Only applicable when destination is
REDIRECT_TUNNEL. Valid range: 1 to 16777215.

tunnel-group.description:
Name of the tunnel group for redirect. Only applicable when
destination is REDIRECT_TUNNEL_GROUP. Maximum 20 characters.

ArubaPolicy_RoutingActionConfig.description:
Grouping for Policy Based Routing (PBR) action configuration.
Defines how matched traffic is routed via nexthop lists, tunnels,
tunnel groups, or IPsec maps.

routing-action.description:
PBR action configuration: dscp tag and routing options for route ACL rules
   - forward: use routing table to forward traffic
   - route:
       - nexthop-list: use nexthop-list to forward traffic
       - tunnel: forward traffic to GRE tunnel
       - tunnel-group: forward traffic to tunnel-group
       - ipsec-map: forward traffic to ipsec tunnel with configured ipsec-map
   - cluster: forward to cluster (only for APs)

destination.description:
PBR nexthop type. This is a required field. NEXTHOP_LIST
routes via a configured nexthop list. IPSEC_MAP routes via
an IPsec tunnel. TUNNEL routes via a GRE tunnel. TUNNEL_GROUP
routes via a tunnel group. FORWARD uses the routing table.

dscp.description:
DSCP tag value to apply to PBR routed traffic.
Valid range: 1-63.

ipsec-map.description:
Name of the IPsec map for PBR routing through an IPsec
tunnel. Only applicable when destination is IPSEC_MAP.
Maximum 256 characters.

next-hop-list.description:
Name of the nexthop list for PBR routing. Only applicable
when destination is NEXTHOP_LIST. References a configured
nexthop group.

tunnel.description:
GRE tunnel ID for PBR routing. Only applicable when
destination is TUNNEL. For gateway devices only.

tunnel-group.description:
Tunnel group name for PBR routing. Only applicable when
destination is TUNNEL_GROUP. For gateway devices only.

ArubaPolicy_RoutingActionConfigGet.description:
Grouping for Policy Based Routing (PBR) action configuration.
Defines how matched traffic is routed via nexthop lists, tunnels,
tunnel groups, or IPsec maps.

routing-action.description:
PBR action configuration: dscp tag and routing options for route ACL rules
   - forward: use routing table to forward traffic
   - route:
       - nexthop-list: use nexthop-list to forward traffic
       - tunnel: forward traffic to GRE tunnel
       - tunnel-group: forward traffic to tunnel-group
       - ipsec-map: forward traffic to ipsec tunnel with configured ipsec-map
   - cluster: forward to cluster (only for APs)

destination.description:
PBR nexthop type. This is a required field. NEXTHOP_LIST
routes via a configured nexthop list. IPSEC_MAP routes via
an IPsec tunnel. TUNNEL routes via a GRE tunnel. TUNNEL_GROUP
routes via a tunnel group. FORWARD uses the routing table.

dscp.description:
DSCP tag value to apply to PBR routed traffic.
Valid range: 1-63.

ipsec-map.description:
Name of the IPsec map for PBR routing through an IPsec
tunnel. Only applicable when destination is IPSEC_MAP.
Maximum 256 characters.

next-hop-list.description:
Name of the nexthop list for PBR routing. Only applicable
when destination is NEXTHOP_LIST. References a configured
nexthop group.

tunnel.description:
GRE tunnel ID for PBR routing. Only applicable when
destination is TUNNEL. For gateway devices only.

tunnel-group.description:
Tunnel group name for PBR routing. Only applicable when
destination is TUNNEL_GROUP. For gateway devices only.

ArubaPolicy_RuleAggregator.description:
Grouping for rule aggregation metadata. Used internally to
group related policy rules by source or destination for
optimized evaluation.

aggregator.description:
Rule aggregation metadata. Groups policy rules by source
or destination address for efficient rule processing.

aggregator-uuid.description:
Unique identifier (UUID) for the aggregation group.
Only applicable when group-type is set.
aggregator-uuid.x-typeDescription:
A Universally Unique IDentifier in the string representation
defined in RFC 4122.  The canonical representation uses
lowercase characters.

The following is an example of a UUID in string representation:
f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6

group-type.description:
Aggregation group type. Value is 'src' to aggregate by
source address or 'dest' to aggregate by destination
address.

ArubaPolicy_SecurityPolicyGroup.description:
Grouping for security policy configuration within a policy.
Contains the rule list, policy-level metadata, and optional
features like CALEA and URL redirection.

security-policy.description:
Security policy configuration for this policy. Contains the
policy type, ordered list of rules, and optional features
such as CALEA lawful intercept and URL redirection.

calea.description:
Enable Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act
(CALEA) lawful intercept on traffic matching this policy.
When true, matching traffic is mirrored for lawful
intercept purposes.

description.description:
A user-defined description or comment for the security
policy. Maximum 256 characters.

redirect-blocked-http-url.description:
When true, HTTP requests that are denied by this policy
are redirected to the configured redirect URL instead of
being silently dropped.

redirect-url.description:
URL to redirect denied HTTP traffic to when
redirect-blocked-http-url is enabled. Maximum 256
characters.

type.description:
Security policy type that determines which protocol fields
are allowed in the policy rules (e.g., IPv4, IPv6,
Ethernet). Affects the valid rule-types for child rules.

x-enumDescriptions.SECURITY_POLICY_TYPE_NETWORK_ENCAP: A special policy created to map network destination for which role-tagging needs to happen

x-enumDescriptions.PROMISCUOUS:
Set port as private-vlan promiscuous port. A promiscuous port
will be a member of the primary VLAN. Promiscuous ports can send
traffic to all ports of the primary VLAN as well as to the ports of
associated isolated/community VLANs. Promiscuous ports are used to
communicate outside the PVLAN domain.
x-enumDescriptions.SECONDARY:
Configure port as private-vlan secondary port. A secondary port will
be a member of a secondary VLAN. Secondary ports which belong to a
community VLAN can send traffic to all ports of the same community
VLAN as well as to the promiscuous ports of its primary VLAN. A port
belonging to an isolated VLAN can only send traffic to promiscuous
ports of its primary VLAN.

fib-optimization-ageout-time.description:
Configures FIB (Forwarding Information Base) Optimization route age-out time.If a host route entry is
designated for ageing, and no traffic is using the route for configured amount of age time, the route
entry will be removed from the ASIC. When traffic using that route resumes,
the route entry will be inserted back to ASIC.

fib-optimization-exclude-nexthop-ipv4.description:
Configures next-hops to be excluded from FIB (Forwarding Information Base) optimization.
User may want to prevent optimization of host routes which resolves to certain next hops.
This leaf-list configures such next hops.Any EVPN host route pointing to the configured next hops,
will not be optimized by the AIF feature.

ArubaBfd_BfdSchemaGET.description:
BFD global configuration.
Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) is a protocol intended to detect
faults in the bidirectional path between two forwarding engines, including
interfaces, data link(s), and to the extent possible the forwarding engines
themselves, with potentially very low latency.  It operates independently of
media, data protocols, and routing protocols.

or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

min-echo-rx-interval.description:
Sets or resets the minimum BFD echo packet reception interval.
The value 0 means that the host is not interested in receiving BFD echo packets.
The value itself is a request to the remote system that it might not be able to
honor (ex. we ask for echo packets faster than it can send them). In this scenario,
the remote system is expected to use its fastest/slowest setting (depending on
what we asked) and the session might flap.

ArubaBgp_BgpGlobalBase.description: Global configuration parameters for the BGP router

confederation.description: BGP Confederation configuration. A BGP Confederation enables dividing a large Autonomous System into smaller sub-AS groups while maintaining the logical appearance of a single AS to external peers. This feature improves scalability by confining iBGP relationships within sub-AS groups while presenting as a single AS externally

default-bgp-attributes.description: Default BGP administrative distance configuration. Administrative Distance (AD) determines route preference when multiple routing protocols offer routes to the same destination. This configuration sets default distance values for routes learned from external BGP (eBGP), internal BGP (iBGP), and locally configured sources. Lower distances indicate higher preference. Typical defaults are: eBGP 20, iBGP 200, local 200

default-originate.description: Originate default route to BGP neighbors

graceful-restart.description: BGP Graceful Restart (GR) mechanism configuration. GR enables high availability during planned and unplanned BGP process restarts by preserving BGP routes and maintaining data plane forwarding while control plane sessions are reestablished. Supporting routers recognize the restart and gracefully handle route withdrawal and re-advertisement, minimizing traffic disruption

max-prefix-options.description:
Parameters relating to the limit for maximum prefix
configuration options.

route-selection-options.description: Route Selection Options for BGP best path computation. Configures BGP best path selection algorithms and tie-breaker rules including AS path length comparison, Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED) handling, route reflector cluster ID behavior, and path origin validation. These options directly influence how BGP selects the preferred path among multiple routes to the same destination, affecting traffic engineering, load balancing, and failover behavior

timers.description: BGP Timers configuration block for controlling BGP session establishment, maintenance, and failure detection. Includes keep-alive timer (frequency of keepalive messages to maintain active sessions), hold-time (maximum time between consecutive BGP messages before session termination), and connect-retry timer (wait time before attempting reconnection after session failure). These timers are critical for tuning BGP convergence speed and network stability

items.x-typeDescription:
A numeric identifier for an autonomous system (AS). An AS is a
single domain, under common administrative control, which forms
a unit of routing policy. Autonomous systems can be assigned a
2-byte identifier, or a 4-byte identifier which may have public
or private scope. Private ASNs are assigned from dedicated
ranges. Public ASNs are assigned from ranges allocated by IANA
to the regional internet registries (RIRs).

ArubaBgp_BgpGlobalGracefulRestart.description: Configuration parameters relating to BGP graceful restart.

graceful-restart-enable.description: Enable graceful restart for BGP instance

restart-time.description:
Estimated time (in seconds) for the local BGP speaker to
restart a session. This value is advertise in the graceful
restart BGP capability.  This is a 12-bit value, referred to
as Restart Time in RFC4724.  Per RFC4724, the suggested
default value is <= the hold-time value.

stale-routes-time.description:
An upper-bound on the time thate stale routes will be
retained by a router after a session is restarted. If an
End-of-RIB (EOR) marker is received prior to this timer
expiring stale-routes will be flushed upon its receipt - if
no EOR is received, then when this timer expires stale paths
will be purged. This timer is referred to as the
Selection_Deferral_Timer in RFC4724

ArubaBgp_BgpGlobalRouteSelectionOptions.description:
Set of configuration options that govern best
path selection.

always-compare-med.description:
Compare multi-exit discriminator (MED) value of the routes
from peers of different ASes when selecting the best route.

as-path-multipath-relax.description:
Consider two or more BGP routes as ECMP routes when
routes AS PATH length is same but AS PATHs are different.

compare-med-confederation.description:
Compare multi-exit discriminator (MED) value of the routes
from peers of different ASes within a confederation when
selecting the best route.

compare-originator-id.description:
When comparing similar routes received from external
BGP peers, use the originator-id as a criterion to select
the active path.

compare-router-id.description:
When comparing similar routes received from external
BGP peers, use the router-id as a criterion to select
the active path.

deterministic-med.description:
Compare multi-exit discriminator (MED) value of the routes
advertised by different peers in the same AS when selecting
the best route.

ignore-as-path-length.description:
Ignore the AS path length when selecting the best path.
The default is to use the AS path length and prefer paths
with shorter length.

med-missing-as-worst.description:
Consider MED value as worst (0xFFFFFFFF), if MED
attribute is missing in the routes when selecting
the best route.

ArubaBgp_BgpNeighborGrouping.description:
Configuration parameters relating to a base BGP neighbor that
are also applicable to peer group context.

as-override.description:
Replace all occurrences of the peer AS number with the
router's own AS number before advertising the route.

auth-password.description:
Configures an MD5 authentication password for use with
neighboring devices.
auth-password.x-typeDescription:
A custom derived type for special use cases. This type takes a plaintext password and uses
Vault's 3rd party API to encrypt the password. The intended use case is to encrypt and store
customer credentials which will be used later to login to 3rd party services.

description.description:
An optional textual description (intended primarily for use
with a peer or group

enabled.description:
Whether the BGP peer is enabled. In cases where the
enabled leaf is set to false, the local system should not
initiate connections to the neighbor, and should not
respond to TCP connections attempts from the neighbor. If
the state of the BGP session is ESTABLISHED at the time
that this leaf is set to false, the BGP session should be
ceased.

fall-over.description: Fall-over the BGP session when route to the peer fails.

fall-over-bfd.description:
Enable BFD session with the neighbor and fall-over the BGP
session when connectivity with the neighbor is lost.

ignore-leading-as.description:
Accept the received routes from the peer even if it does
not have their own AS appended to the as-path.

local-as.description:
The local autonomous system number that is to be used
when establishing sessions with the remote peer or peer
group, if this differs from the global BGP router
autonomous system number.

local-as-mode.description: The different modes of using ASN as local AS.

x-enumDescriptions.NO_PREPEND:
The session is established via alternate local-as.
Both the alternate-as and primary-as are not prepended to the inbound AS_PATH list,
but prepended to the outbound AS_PATH list.
x-enumDescriptions.NO_PREPEND_REPLACE_AS:
The session is established via alternate local-as.
Both the alternate-as and primary-as are not prepended to the inbound AS_PATH list,
but alternate local-as is prepended to the outbound AS_PATH list.
x-enumDescriptions.NO_PREPEND_REPLACE_AS_DUAL_AS:
The session can be established using either primary-as or alternate local-as.
Selected-as is not prepended to the inbound AS_PATH list,
but prepended to outbound AS_PATH list.

local-as-mode.x-typeDescription: The modes of using specified ASN as local AS for forming BGP sessions with peers.

remove-private-as.description:
Remove private AS numbers from updates sent to peers - when
this leaf is not specified, the AS_PATH attribute should be
sent to the peer unchanged

use-med.description:
Enable the comparison of MED attribute for the same route
received from two different autonomous systems.

weight.description: This is the weight for routes from this neighbor.

ArubaBgp_BgpSchemaGET.description:
Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is the standard exterior gateway
protocol (RFC 4271) for exchanging routing information between
autonomous systems on the Internet and enterprise networks. BGP
supports IPv4/IPv6 unicast, EVPN (Ethernet VPN), and multicast
address families with advanced features including route reflection,
confederation, graceful restart, and multi-path load balancing.
Configure BGP global parameters, neighbor relationships, route
redistribution, and address family-specific policies. Requires route
map, prefix list, keychain, and community list configurations for
routing policy enforcement. Use this API to retrieve BGP
configuration.

profile.description:
BGP routing profile containing a single router instance per
Autonomous System. Each entity is identified by profile name.
Configure AS number, VRF instances, neighbors, route policies,
timers, and address families. Use these APIs to create, modify, or
delete a BGP profile.

platform-type.description: Type of the platform (GW, PVOS, CX).
platform-type.x-typeDescription: This value represents the type of Aruba platform.

router.description: BGP Router instance. Each BGP profile supports only ONE router instance (single Autonomous System). The router is identified by a unique AS number that must be consistent across the profile. Multiple AS numbers are not allowed within the same BGP profile. Each instance contains complete BGP configuration including neighbor/peer relationships (internal iBGP and external eBGP), routing policies, keepalive/hold timers, address family configurations (IPv4, IPv6, VPNv4), graceful restart, route reflection, and best path selection

ArubaCommunityList_CommunityListsSchemaG.description: BGP Community Lists configuration. A BGP Community is a 32-bit value used to classify and group routes for policy application. This container manages three types of Community Lists: Standard (specific community values), Expanded (regular expression patterns), and Extended (route targets and extended community formats). Each list contains ordered entries with permit or deny actions for route classification and policy enforcement

community-list.description: BGP Community List definition with a unique name and type specification. ArubaEvpn_EvpnArpNdProxyConfig.description: Configuration data related to ARP-Proxy and ND-Proxy

arp-suppression.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

arp-suppression-extended.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with arp-suppression.
Basically arp-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of arp-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

nd-suppression.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

nd-suppression-extended.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with nd-suppression.
Basically nd-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of nd-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

The number of MAC mobility events that are detected for a
given MAC address within the detection-window before it is identified
as a duplicate MAC address. Once the detection threshold is reached,
updates for the MAC address are suppressed.

The time interval used in detecting a duplicate MAC address.
The value can be from 1 through 1000 seconds.

virtual-links.description:
In Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), a virtual link is a logical path that
connects areas of a network that are not physically connected.
Virtual links are used when it's not possible to connect all areas
of an OSPFv2 autonomous system to the backbone area (area 0).
They can also be used to connect two parts of a partitioned backbone.

Virtual links cannot be configured through backbone area or stub/nssa area.

ArubaOspfv2_Ospfv2SchemaGET.description:
OSPFv2 (Open Shortest Path First version 2) is a routing protocol which is
described in RFC2328 entitled OSPF Version 2. It is a Link State-based
IGP(Interior Gateway Protocol) routing protocol. It is widely used in medium
to large-sized enterprise networks.

The characteristics of OSPFv2 are:

- Provides a loop free topology using SPF algorithm.
- Allows hierarchical routing using area 0 (backbone area) as the top of the
 hierarchy.
- Supports load balancing with equal cost routes for same destination.
- OSPFv2 is a classless protocol and allows for a hierarchical design with
 VLSM(Variable length subnet masking) and route summarization.
- Provides authentication of routing messages.
- Scales enterprise size network easily with area concept.
- Provides fast convergence with triggered, incremental updates via
 Link State Advertisements (LSAs).

profile.description: OSPFv2 configuration profiles for organizing router instances.

description.description: Description of the OSPFv2 profile purpose and configuration.

name.description: Profile name for the OSPFv2 configuration group.

routers.description: The list of all the OSPFv2 Router instances.

areas.description:
The list of all the OSPF area for the OSPF router instance.

An area in OSPF is a logical collection of routers, links and
OSPF networks that have the same area ID. Areas are used to divide
an OSPF network into sub-domains. The main benefit of creating areas
is that it reduces the number of routes that need to be propagated.

backbone-stub-default-route.description: Advertise default route to stub if loopback in backbone area.

default-information-origin.description:
Generate a default external route into an ospfv2 routing domain.
Only one among 'always', 'metric', 'always-metric' can be configured

distance.description:
OSPFv2 distance.

Administrative Distance is used as criteria to select the source of the
route when the same route is learned from different routing protocols.
Optionally, Administrative Distance can be set for each OSPFv3 route type
intra-area, inter-area, and external type-5 and type-7 routes.

distribute-filter.description:
Used to filter routes from being installed in the routing table or
redistributed into another routing protocol.
When inbound direction is used it filter routes to be installed in the routing table.
Outbound direction will filter only the desired redistributed routes from other protocols.
The prefix-list which is provided in command will be used to filter routes for both
inbound and outbound direction. Configuration is not allowed if the referenced
prefix-list has not yet been configured.

prefix.description: Prevent redistribution of routes via OSPF.

(0 <= mask <= 128).

graceful-restart-cfg.description:
Graceful restart OSPF.
If `strict-lsa-check` option is mentioned, the router
will not perform strict LSA check when acting as a restart helper
for a restarting peer. By default, router will participate
in the graceful restart of a neighbor with strict LSA check enabled.

instance-tag-vrf.description: Key combination of instance-tag and vrf separated by ~

max-metric.description:
sets the protocol to advertise a maximum metric so that other
routers do not prefer the router as an intermediate hop in their shortest
path first (SPF) calculations.
- `include-stub` option configures the router to advertise maximum
  metric for links including stub links in router LSA.
- `on-startup` option configures the router to advertise maximum metric in
  router LSA at startup for the time mentioned in seconds or for
  a default value of 600 seconds.
- `include-stub` and `on-startup` options together configure the router
  to advertise maximum metric for links including stub links in router LSA at
  startup for the time mentioned in seconds or for a default value of 600 seconds.

but still participates in the routing process for subnet advertisement.

connects areas of a network that are not physically connected.
Virtual links are used when it's not possible to connect all areas

ArubaOspfv3_Ospfv3SchemaGET.description:
OSPFv3 (Open Shortest Path First version 3) is a routing protocol which is
described in RFC5340 entitled OSPF for IPv6. It is a Link State-based IGP
(Interior Gateway Protocol) routing protocol. It is widely used with medium to
large-sized enterprise networks.

The characteristics of OSPFv3 are:

- Provides a loop free topology using SPF algorithm.
- Allows hierarchical routing using area 0 (backbone area) as the top of the
  hierarchy.
- Supports load balancing with equal cost routes for same destination.
- OSPFv3 is a classless protocol and allows for a hierarchical design with
  VLSM (Variable Length Subnet Masking) and route summarization.
- Scales enterprise size network easily with area concept.
- Provides fast convergence with triggered, incremental updates via
  Link State Advertisements (LSAs).

active-backbone-stub.description: Advertise default route to stub if loopback in backbone area.

areas.description:
The list of all the OSPFv3 area for the OSPFv3 router instance.

An area in OSPFv3 is a logical collection of routers, links and
OSPFv3 networks that have the same area ID. Areas are used to divide
an OSPFv3 network into sub-domains. The main benefit of creating areas
is that it reduces the number of routes that need to be propagated.

default-info-originate.description:
Generate a default external route into an ospfv2 routing domain.
Only one among 'always', 'metric', 'always-metric' can be configured

distance.description:
OSPFv3 distance.

Administrative Distance is used as criteria to select the source of the
route when the same route is learned from different routing protocols.
Optionally, Administrative Distance can be set for each OSPFv3 route type
intra-area, inter-area, and external type-5 and type-7 routes.

prefix.description: Prevent redistribution of routes via OSPF.
prefix.x-typeDescription:
An IPv6 prefix represented in full, shortened, or mixed
shortened format followed by a slash and CIDR mask
(0 <= mask <= 128).

graceful-restart-cfg.description:
Graceful restart OSPF.
If `strict-lsa-check` option is mentioned, the router
will not perform strict LSA check when acting as a restart helper
for a restarting peer. By default, router will participate
in the graceful restart of a neighbor with strict LSA check enabled.

instance-tag-vrf.description: Key combination of instance-tag and vrf separated by ~

max-metric.description:
sets the protocol to advertise a maximum metric so that other
routers do not prefer the router as an intermediate hop in their shortest
path first (SPF) calculations.
- `include-stub` option configures the router to advertise maximum
  metric for links including stub links in router LSA.
- `on-startup` option configures the router to advertise maximum metric in
  router LSA at startup for the time mentioned in seconds or for
  a default value of 600 seconds.
- `include-stub` and `on-startup` options together configure the router
  to advertise maximum metric for links including stub links in router LSA at
  startup for the time mentioned in seconds or for a default value of 600 seconds.

maximum-paths.description: Maximum number of equal cost paths that are stored for each destination in the Routing table.

x-enumDescriptions.TYPE1: Comparable (an OSPFv3 metric plus the external metric)

nonstop.description: Enables or disables nonstop forwarding for OSPFv3.

passive-interface-default.description:
All OSPFv3 enabled interfaces to be passive.
An OSPFv3 passive interface is a network interface
that does not send or receive OSPFv3 Hello packets,
but still participates in the routing process for subnet advertisement.

reference-bandwidth.description: The reference bandwidth, Mbits/second, for interface cost calculations.

restrict-routes.description: Restrict redistribution of routes via OSPF.

items.description: Restrict redistribution of routes via OSPF.

An IPv6 prefix represented in full, shortened, or mixed
shortened format followed by a slash and CIDR mask

route-filter.description:
Used to filter routes from being installed in the routing table or
redistributed into another routing protocol.
When inbound direction is used it filter routes to be installed in the routing table.
Outbound direction will filter only the desired redistributed routes from other protocols.
The prefix-list which is provided in command will be used to filter routes for both
inbound and outbound direction. Configuration is not allowed if the referenced
prefix-list has not yet been configured.

router-id.description: The router identifier for the OSPFv3 instance.
router-id.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

summary-aggregate-route.description:
Summarizes the external routes with the matching address or masks.
When advertising this route, its, metric would be set to the lowest
cost path from among the routes that were summarized.
With no-advertise flag enabled, Suppress routes that match the
specified prefix/mask pair.
Only works for ASBR(Autonomous System Boundary Router).

ArubaPim_PimRouterSchemaGET.description:
Configure Protocol Independent Multicast.
In a network, IP multicast traffic transmitted for multimedia applications
is blocked at routed interface boundaries unless a multicast routing protocol
is running. Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) is a family of routing
protocols. It forms multicast trees to forward traffic from multicast sources
to the clients requesting for traffic.

Allow same multicast source to be directly connected
to two or more Anycast RP routers on IPv4 network

candidate-bsr.description:
Candidate Bootstrap Router Configuration for IPv4 network.
A candidate BSR is configured so that it is eligible to be elected as the
Bootstrap Router (BSR) in a PIM domain. This is the router that collects
information from all available RPs in the network and advertises it on the
PIM domain.

candidate-bsr-v6.description: Candidate Bootstrap Router Configuration for IPv6 network

candidate-rp.description:
Candidate RP Configuration for IPv4 network.
A candidate RP is configured to take part in the rendezvous point(RP) election in
PIM Sparse Mode(SM). To become an RP, a candidate RP will announce itself to the
bootstrap router (BSR) using unicast packets.

ArubaPrefixList_PrefixListsSchemaGET.description:
Prefix Lists are standard routing filters (RFC 4632) used to permit
or deny network routes based on IP address prefixes in CIDR notation.
Configure IPv4 and IPv6 prefix lists for granular route control in
BGP and OSPF routing policies. Each list contains sequential entries
with permit/deny actions and optional prefix length matching
constraints for flexible route filtering across multi-site networks.

characters. Use this API to retrieve the list of prefix list
configurations.

ArubaRip_RipSchemaGET.description:
Routing Information Protocol (RIP) is a distance-vector interior
gateway protocol (IGP) using hop count as the routing metric
with a maximum of 15 hops (RFC 2453). RIP supports RIPv1 and
RIPv2 for IPv4 networks with features including route
redistribution, authentication, route filtering, and
configurable timers. Configure RIP router instances with
administrative distance, maximum paths, timers (update,
timeout, garbage-collection), route redistribution from other
protocols, and interface-specific parameters. Use this API to
retrieve the list of RIP profiles.

profile.description:
RIP routing profile defining router instances, redistribution
rules, timers, administrative distance, and interface
configurations. Each entity is identified by profile name.
Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete a RIP profile
instance.
