ArubaRoutemap_RouteMapSet.description: Route-map Set Actions configuration. Provides comprehensive tools for manipulating routing protocol attributes and traffic policies. This container supports setting BGP Path Attributes (AS path prepending/exclusion, communities, origin, local preference, MED), OSPF metrics, tag-based traffic classification, and next-hop address overrides. Set actions enable sophisticated traffic engineering, route filtering policies, and attribute-based routing across BGP, OSPF, and other routing protocols

set-as-path.description: Modify BGP AS Path attribute. Allows prepending additional Autonomous System numbers (for increasing local preference) or excluding specific AS numbers (for path filtering). AS Path manipulation is fundamental to BGP traffic engineering and helps control route propagation patterns and neighbor selection behavior

as-exclude.description: Set AS to be excluded from AS-path.

last-as-prepend-count.description: Number of times to prepend the last AS to AS path attribute

prepend-as.description: Space-separated list of Autonomous System numbers to prepend to the route's AS path. Prepending increases the AS path length, making routes less preferred during BGP best path selection. Used for traffic engineering to influence incoming traffic direction. Each AS number in the list is prepended once in the order specified. Example: 65000 65001 (prepends AS 65000, then AS 65001)

set-community.description: BGP Community Attribute configuration. Enables setting or modifying BGP Community values to classify routes for policy application. Supports standard communities (AS:value pairs), extended communities (for VPNs), and well-known communities (INTERNET, NO_EXPORT, NO_ADVERTISE, LOCAL_AS). Community operations include additive (append) and delete (remove specific communities)

items.description: Community attribute value.

set-community-list.description: BGP community list attribute to be set

set-dampening.description: Configurations related to Routemap for Route-flap dampening

half-life.description:
Amount of time that must elapse to reduce
the penalty by one half.

max-suppress-time.description: The maximum amount of time that a route can be suppressed.

reuse-limit.description: Penalty value at which routes are made active.

suppress-limit.description:
If the penalty is greater than the suppress limit,
 the route is suppressed.

set-extended-community.description: Configurations related to setting IP extended communities.

items.description: Set route-target extended community.

router-mac.description: Set the Router MAC address extended community.
router-mac.x-typeDescription:
The mac-address type represents an IEEE 802 MAC address.
The canonical representation uses lowercase characters.

In the value set and its semantics, this type is equivalent
to the MacAddress textual convention of the SMIv2.

set-ipv4-nexthop-address.description: IPv4 next-hop address to be set for BGP routes. Overrides the default next-hop address used for routes matched by this route-map entry. Useful for policy-based route manipulation and traffic engineering to force traffic through specific next-hops or gateways. Cannot be combined with IPv6 configuration
set-ipv4-nexthop-address.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

set-ipv6-nexthop.description: IPv6 global next-hop address to be set for BGP routes. Overrides the default next-hop address used for IPv6 routes matched by this route-map entry. Used for policy-based route manipulation, traffic engineering, and IPv6 path selection. Cannot be combined with IPv4 configuration
set-ipv6-nexthop.x-typeDescription:
An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

set-local-broadcast-group.description: Set the local broadcast group id.

set-local-preference.description: BGP Local Preference attribute value to be set. Local Preference influences route selection within the local Autonomous System (all iBGP neighbors see the same value). Higher values indicate more preferred routes; routes to the same destination are compared and the route with highest local preference is selected. Default value is 100. Used for traffic engineering within your AS

set-metric.description: BGP Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED) attribute value to be set (also called metric). MED is used to influence route selection between external BGP (eBGP) neighbors in a specific AS. Lower MED values are more preferred. Unlike Local Preference, MED is advertised to external peers. Used for traffic engineering to external neighbors to indicate preferred entry points

set-origin.description: BGP Origin attribute value to be set. The Origin attribute indicates how the route was learned: IGP (Interior Gateway Protocol - learned from internal protocol like OSPF), EGP (Exterior Gateway Protocol - rare legacy usage), or Incomplete (origin unknown - common for redistributed or statically configured routes). Used in BGP best path selection as a tie-breaker

set-tag.description: Route Tag attribute. A 32-bit numeric tag value assigned to routes for classification, filtering, and tracking across routing domains. Tags are used in OSPF, static routing, and policy-based routing for route discrimination and policy application. Tags enable route identification without protocol-specific attributes

set-weight.description: BGP Weight attribute value to be set. Routes with higher weight values are preferred during BGP best path selection (weight comparison occurs before AS path length comparison). Weight has local AS significance only and is not advertised to neighbors. Default weight is 32768

ArubaRoutemap_RouteMapsSchemaGET.description:
Route Maps provide advanced routing policy control by
manipulating route attributes during redistribution between
routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, RIP, static routes). Route
maps use match conditions (IP prefix lists, community lists,
AS path lists) and set actions (metric modification,
next-hop changes, AS path prepending) to filter and transform
routing information. Configure route map sequences with
permit/deny actions to implement complex routing policies for
traffic engineering and route aggregation. Requires
prefix-list, community-list, and AS path-list configurations
for match conditions. Device Limits: Gateway restricts route
map names to 1-50 characters. Use this API to retrieve the
list of route map configurations.

route-map.description:
Route map defining policy-based route manipulation with
ordered sequences of match conditions and set actions.
Each entity is identified by route map name. Configure
permit/deny entries with match criteria (prefix-lists,
communities, AS paths) and set actions (metric, next-hop,
local-preference) for routing policy control.

ArubaStaticRoute_StaticRouteSchemaGET.description:
Static routing is a type of network routing technique. Static routing is
not a routing protocol; instead, it is the manual configuration and
selection of a network route, usually managed by the network administrator.
It is employed in scenarios where the network routing parameters are not

ArubaVrf_VrfsSchemaGET.description: Virtual Routing Forwarding (VRF) container. A VRF is a logical partition of a network device's routing infrastructure that enables multiple independent routing tables on a single device. This container manages VRF instances, each with isolated routing domains, independent routing policies, route targets, and address families (IPv4, IPv6). VRFs support multi-tenancy, network segregation, and route leaking capabilities (IVRL - Inter-VRF Route Leaking) for complex network architectures

vrf.description: List of named VRF instances. Each VRF maintains independent routing tables and policy enforcement domains. The 'default' VRF represents the global routing table. Each VRF can be associated with specific route targets for inter-VRF route leaking, enabling controlled route distribution across VRF boundaries for overlay and VPN deployments

Aruba802dot11kBcnRptReq_BcnRptReqProfile.description:
The Beacon Report Requests are sent only to 802.11k-compliant clients that advertise Beacon Report Capability in their
Radio Measurement (RM) Enabled Capabilities Information Element (IE).
This includes configuring BSSID, Channel, Measurement Mode, Regulatory Class, etc.

profile.description:
Configures list of Beacon Report Request Profile to provide the parameters for the Beacon Report Request frames.
The Beacon Report Request profile is attached to 802.11K profile.

bssid.description: BSSID included in the beacon request. Default: wildcard

channel.description:
This option is used to set the Channel field in the Beacon Report Request frame. The Channel value can be set to one of the following:
The channel of the AP (when Measurement Mode is set to either 'Passive' or 'Active-All channels') 0 (when Measurement Mode is set to 'Beacon Table')
255 (when Measurement Mode is set to 'Active-Channel Report')

oneOf.x-typeDescription: 2.4GHz radio channel list
5GHz radio channel list
6GHz radio channel list

x-enumDescriptions.ZERO_CHAN_FOR_ZERO: some times 0 is also an valid input

oneOf.x-typeDescription: Channel 0/255 for all channels

include-ssid.description: Enable including SSID IE in Beacon Report Request

last-beacon-rpt-indication.description: Enable Last Beacon Request Indication sub-element in Beacon Report Request.

measure-duration.description:
Measurement Duration field in the Beacon Report Request frame.
The Measurement Duration is set to the duration of the requested measurement. It is expressed in units of TUs.

measure-mode.description: Measurement Mode for Beacon Reports. The mode should be one of active-all-ch|active-ch-rpt|beacon-table|passive. Default: beacon-table
measure-mode.x-typeDescription: Indicates the mode used for the measurement.

random-interval.description:
Randomization Interval field in the Beacon Report Request frame.
The Randomization Interval is used to specify the desired maximum random delay in the measurement start time.
It is expressed in units of TUs (Time Units). A Randomization Interval of 0 in a measurement request indicates that
no random delay is to be used.

reg-class.description: Regulatory Class for Beacon Report Request. Value: auto, 1, 12, 81, 115, or 131. Default auto to use value based on country code

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO: Auto uses value based on country code.

Contents of the Request Information IE that could be present in the Beacon Report Request frame.
The Request Information IE is present for all Measurement Modes except the Beacon Table mode. It consists of a list of Element IDs that
should be included by the client in the response frame.
Any valid element ID in the x/y/z format. For example, 0/21/22.

Aruba802dot11k_Dot11kProfilesSchemaGET.description:
The 802.11k protocol provides mechanisms for APs and clients to dynamically measure the available radio resources.
In an 802.11k enabled network, APs and clients can send neighbor reports, beacon reports, and link measurement reports to each other.
This allows the APs and clients to take appropriate connection actions.
This includes configuring channel-report, reference of Beacon Report Request profile and RRM IE Profile, etc.

ArubaAaaCaptivePortal_CaptivePortalSchem.description:
Use this API to configure external captive portal profiles for guest users. For AP and GW, When the captive portal profile is applied to an SSID or a wired profile, the users connecting
to the SSID or wired network are assigned a role with the captive portal rule. For CX, when the client is 802.1x or MAC authenticated through RADIUS-server, the redirect parameters in this
profile can be applied through user-role, Downloadable User Role and RADIUS Vendor Specific Attribute. This feature is applicable for AP, CX and GW.

items.description: Allow List of Netdestinations.

ap-mac-in-redirection-url.description: Add AP's MAC address in redirection URL.

apple-cna-bypass.description: To bypass Apple CNA on iOS devices like iPad, iPhone, iPod.

auth-text.description:
Configures the authentication text to be returned by the external server. The authentication text command configuration is
required only for the External Authentication Text splash mode.

auto-allowlist.description: Disables automatic whitelisting / allowlisting of URLs.

items.description: Deny List of Netdestinations.

description.description: Description, or comment, for the Captive Portal profile.

enable-welcome-page.description: Enable the welcome page before redirection to original destination.

external-cp-server-url.description: The URL for the external captive portal server, URL format:http(s)://<server>:<port>/path.

ip-addr-in-redirection-url.description: Add one of the controller interfaces in the redirection URL.

logon-wait-cpu-threshold.description: Logon wait when CPU is overloaded, CPU utilization threshold (%). Range: 1-100. Default: 60.

logon-wait-max-delay.description: Logon wait when CPU is overloaded,Maximum wait (secs).

logon-wait-min-delay.description: Logon wait when CPU is overloaded, minimum wait (secs).

logout-popup-window.description: Open popup window for logout after authentication.

max-authentication-failures.description: Maximum auth failures before user is added to denylist.Range: 0-10. Default: 0.

name.description: The name of the captive portal profile.

out-of-service-page.description: Configures a URL to redirect the users when the internet uplink is down.

prevent-frame-overlay.description: When the Prevent frame overlay option is enabled, a frame can display a page only if it is in the same domain as the main page.

redirect-pause.description: Pause time for automatic redirect.Range: 1-60, 0 to disable. Default: 10.

redirect-url.description: Specify a redirect URL to redirect users to another URL.
redirect-url.x-typeDescription:
An ASCII-encoded Uniform Resource Locator (URL) as defined
in RFC 3986, section 1.1.3

server-failthrough.description: Allow the guest clients to access Internet when the external captive portal server is not available.

server-offload.description: Enables the server-offload feature to reduce the load on the external captive portal server by allowing the Instant AP to use a Meta tag to redirect HTTP and HTTPS requests from the client.

show-acceptable-use-policy.description: Show the acceptable use policy page before the logon page.

ArubaAaaDot1xauth_Dot1xauthSchemaGET.description:
IEEE 802.1X is an IEEE Standard for port-based Network Access Control (PNAC).
This standard provides an authentication mechanism to devices wishing to attach
to a LAN or WLAN.
IEEE 802.1X defines the encapsulation of the Extensible Authentication Protocol
(EAP) over IEEE 802, which is known as EAP over LAN (EAPOL).

802.1X authentication involves three entities, a supplicant, an authenticator,
and an authentication server.

*Supplicant*: An entity that wants to get authenticated.
*Authenticator*: A network device, such as an Ethernet switch that authenticates
the Supplicant.
*Authentication Server*: Typically a host running software supporting the RADIUS
and EAP protocols that provides an authentication service to an authenticator.

Until the Supplicant is authenticated, 802.1X Authenticator allows only EAPOL
traffic through the port to which the Supplicant is connected.
Only after the authentication is successful, the authenticator allows normal
traffic from the Supplicant.

ArubaAaaStatefulDot1x_StatefulDot1xProfi.description:
Condigure a Stateful 802.1X profile.
This feature when enabled allows the controller to learn the identity and role of a user connected to a third-party AP,
and is useful for authenticating users to networks with APs from multiple vendors. This has been widely used in
SDWAN branch gateways to learn the roles of clients connected to IAP. When any 801.1X authenticator sends RADIUS request to server,
gateway inspects this request and its response from server to learn about the authentication state of the user. Gateway then applies an
identity-based user role to the device

ArubaAuthServerGroup_ServerGroupsSchemaG.description:
Allow you to manage a configured authentication server to an ordered list in a server group, for AP and GW you can configure server rules to derive a user role,
VLAN ID or VLAN name from attributes returned by the server during authentication.
For CX, A maximum of 32 AAA server-groups are supported. Out of these four are default server-groups (local, none, radius, tacacs) and the rest 28 can be user configured.
For AP, A maximum of 16 AAA server-groups are supported for per device. And all server-groups can be user configured.
This feature is applicable for all devices.

with the next server in the list. The device attempts authentication with each server in the ordered list until either there is a successful
authentication or the list of servers in the group is exhausted.

ArubaAuthServer_AuthServersSchemaGET.description:
Use this API to configure an external RADIUS server for user authentication. You can configure parameters such as server IP, authentication port, accounting port,
shared key, etc. This feature is applicable for all devices.

acct-modifier.description:
Attributes modifier for accounting-request.
this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

acct-port.description:
Port number for accounting requests.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.
acct-port.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

admin-dn.description:
DN for the admin user who has read or search privileges across all of the entries in the LDAP database (the user does not need
write privileges but should be able to search the database and read attributes of other users in the database).
This field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

admin-password.description:
Password for the admin user.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.
admin-password.x-typeDescription:
A custom derived type for special use cases. This type takes a plaintext password and uses
Vault's 3rd party API to encrypt the password. The intended use case is to encrypt and store
customer credentials which will be used later to login to 3rd party services.

allow-cleartext.description:
Allow unencrypted communication with LDAP server.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

auth-modifier.description:
Attributes modifier for authentication-request.
this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

auth-port.description:
Port number for authentication requests.For CX, default auth-port for RADIUS Servers is 1812 and TACACS Servers is 49.
For CX and PVOS, this parameter cannot be modified.
auth-port.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

auth-server-address.description: IP address or FQDN of the Auth server. For CX and PVOS, auth-server-address is a mandatory parameter and can not be modified.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

auth-throttle.description: AP measures request-response times for each packet exchange. As the time taken approaches the timeout, AP throttles new transactions.

authentication-type.description:
Specifies authentication protocol which is used for communication with Auth servers.
If not specified, the global timeout value will be picked. This field can be configured only when type is TACACS OR RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

base-dn.description:
DN name of the node which contains the entire user database to use.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

chase-referrals.description:
LDAP Chase Referrals.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

cppm-password-config.description:
Auth server Clearpass password configuration used for authentication.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

cppm-user-name.description:
User name of the ClearPass server to authenticate.
For CX, supported length is 2-64.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

deadtime.description:
Configures a dead time interval for the authentication server. When two or more authentication servers are configured on the Instant AP and
a server is unavailable, the dead time configuratidetermines the duration for which the authentication server would be available if the server
is marked as unavailable. the default value is 5min. time range is 1-1440.

default-authenticated-role.description:
Assign default role for users after XML server
 authorization.

domain.description:
Windows domain name.
this field can be configured only when type is WINDOWS.

gateway.description: Gateway IP address of the DRP VLAN

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

ip.description: IP address to be used as source IP for RADIUS packets and subnet mask of the DRP IP address.
ip.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 prefix represented in dotted quad notation followed by
a slash and a CIDR mask (0 <= mask <= 32).

vlan.description: VLAN in which the RADIUS packets are sent.

dynamic-authorization-port.description: Configures the port number for sending AirGroup CoA, instead of the standard CoA port. The default value is 5999.
dynamic-authorization-port.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

enable-radsec.description:
Enables RadSec for RADIUS data transport over TCP and TLS
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS.
For CX and PVOS, this parameter cannot be modified.

enable-radsec-pcap.description:
Enables RadSec packet capture
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS.

event-timestamp-required.description:
Discard DAC request, if Event-Timestamp is not present
in DAC(Dynamic Authorization Client) request. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as COA_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

filter.description:
Filter that should be applied to search of the user in the LDAP database.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP

ipsec-ah.description:
RADIUS server IPsec authentication parameters.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

ipsec-esp.description:
RADIUS server IPsec encryption parameters.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

encryption-key.description:
The plaintext key for IPsec encryption.
This field can be configured only when encryption-key-type is PLAIN_TEXT.

encryption-key-cipher-text.description:
The ciphertext key for IPsec encryption.
This field can be configured only when encryption-key-type is CIPHER_TEXT.

encryption-key-hexstring.description:
The hex-string key for IPsec encryption.
This field can be configured only when encryption-key-type is HEX_STRING.

encryption-key-type.description: The key type for IPsec encryption.

x-enumDescriptions.CIPHER_TEXT: Configure ciphertext type of IPsec key
x-enumDescriptions.HEX_STRING: Configure hex-string type of IPsec key
x-enumDescriptions.PLAIN_TEXT: Configure plaintext type of IPsec key

encryption-key-type.x-typeDescription: The key type for the IPsec authentication or the IPsec encryption.

encryption-type.description: Specify the algorithm to use for IPsec encryption: aes, des or 3des.

The attribute that should be used as a key in search
for the LDAP server. This field can be configured only when type is LDAP

lower-case-mac-address.description:

This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

mac-address-delimiter.description:
MAC address delimiter.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

management-interface.description: Out of Band management interface for the Auth server.

max-connection.description:
Maximum number of simultaneous non-admin connections to a LDAP server.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP

max-retransmit-attempts.description:
Maximum number of retries sent to the server by the manager device(AP, GW and SW_CX) before the server is marked as down.
For AP, the default value is 3.
For CX, range is 0-5. If not specified, the global retry value will be picked.

msg-auth-required.description:
Enforcement of RADIUS message authenticator. if AP receives Access-Request/Access-Reject/Access-Challenge/CoA-Request/Disconnect-Request without message-authenticator present, the packet will be discarded.
For AP, this configuration is supported from 10.7.1.0.
this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS

name.description: The name of the Auth Server.

nas-identifier.description:
NAS identifier to use in RADIUS packets.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

nas-ip-address.description: The NAS IP address to be sent in RADIUS packets from that server.

RadSec port-access tunnel active

Specifies the mode in which the RADIUS server is used.
- AUTH_ONLY: Server is used only for authentication.
- COA_ONLY: Server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).
- AUTH_AND_COA: Server is used for both authentication and CoA.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTH_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for authentication.
x-enumDescriptions.COA_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).

rfc5997.description:
When enabled, this parameter allows the Instant AP to send a status-server request to determine the actual status of the authentication or accounting server. This proves useful when there is a authentication or request time
rfc5997—RFC5997 support enabled for both authentication and accounting on the authentication server.

write privileges but should be able to search the database and read attributes of other users in the database).
This field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

admin-password.description:
Password for the admin user.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.
admin-password.x-typeDescription:
A custom derived type for special use cases. This type takes a plaintext password and uses
Vault's 3rd party API to encrypt the password. The intended use case is to encrypt and store
customer credentials which will be used later to login to 3rd party services.

allow-cleartext.description:
Allow unencrypted communication with LDAP server.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

auth-modifier.description:
Attributes modifier for authentication-request.
this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

auth-port.description:
Port number for authentication requests.For CX, default auth-port for RADIUS Servers is 1812 and TACACS Servers is 49.
For CX and PVOS, this parameter cannot be modified.
auth-port.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

auth-server-address.description: IP address or FQDN of the Auth server. For CX and PVOS, auth-server-address is a mandatory parameter and can not be modified.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

auth-throttle.description: AP measures request-response times for each packet exchange. As the time taken approaches the timeout, AP throttles new transactions.

base-dn.description:
DN name of the node which contains the entire user database to use.
this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

chase-referrals.description:

this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

cppm-password-config.description:

this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

x-enumDescriptions.LDAP_S: set preferred connection type as LDAP-S

radius-server-mode.description:
Specifies the mode in which the RADIUS server is used.
- AUTH_ONLY: Server is used only for authentication.
- COA_ONLY: Server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).
- AUTH_AND_COA: Server is used for both authentication and CoA.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTH_AND_COA: RADIUS server is used for both authentication and CoA.
x-enumDescriptions.AUTH_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for authentication.
x-enumDescriptions.COA_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).

radsec-client-cert.description:
RADIUS Security Client Certificate Name.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

radsec-est-cert-profile.description:
RADIUS Security Server Certificate Name.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS and radius-server-mode is equal to COA_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

rfc5997.description:
When enabled, this parameter allows the Instant AP to send a status-server request to determine the actual status of the authentication or accounting server. This proves useful when there is a authentication or request time
rfc5997—RFC5997 support enabled for both authentication and accounting on the authentication server.
auth-only—RFC5997 support enabled for authentication only.
acct-only—RFC5997 support enabled for accounting only
no rfc5997—Disables RFC5997 support for the authentication server.

x-enumDescriptions.ACCT_ONLY: Query Status of Acct RADIUS Servers.
x-enumDescriptions.AUTH_ONLY: Query Status of Auth RADIUS Servers.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: Query Status of auth and accounting RADIUS Servers.

rfc5997.x-typeDescription: Query Status of auth and accounting RADIUS Servers.

Change Service Type default value to framed.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

x-enumDescriptions.FRAMED: Change Service-Type default value to framed for CP and MAC auth.
x-enumDescriptions.STANDARD: Follow RFC, the default Service-Type for 802.1x is framed, for CP is Login, for mac is Call-Back.

service-type.x-typeDescription: Change the default value of service type.

service-type-frame-1x.description: Change Service-Type value to frame for 802.1x.

timeout.description:
Maximum time, in seconds, that the manager device(AP, GW and SW_CX) waits before timing out the request and resending it.
For CX, range is 1-60. If not specified, the global timeout value will be picked.
For AP, the default value of RADIUS and LDAP is 5, TACACS is 20.

TLS Initial connection timeout (timeout for TLS handshake).
For CX, if not specified, the global TLS Initial connection timeout value will be picked.

tracking-method.description:

x-enumDescriptions.ACCESS_REQUEST: Track the server using access-request messages

x-enumDescriptions.TCP_KEEPALIVE: Track the server using TCP keep-alive messages

This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

x-enumDescriptions.ANY: Track the server irrespective of its availability.
x-enumDescriptions.DEAD_ONLY: Track the server only if it is not reachable.

radius-server-mode.description:
Specifies the mode in which the RADIUS server is used.
- AUTH_ONLY: Server is used only for authentication.
- COA_ONLY: Server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).
- AUTH_AND_COA: Server is used for both authentication and CoA.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTH_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for authentication.
x-enumDescriptions.COA_ONLY: RADIUS server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA).

radsec-est-cert-profile.description:
RADIUS Security Server Certificate Name.
This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

radsec-keepalive.description: If there is no radius activity for more than 15 minutes, with status-server keepalive, CPPM doesn't terminate connection every 15 minutes, with tcp-keepalive , CPPM terminates the RADSEC connection after 15 minutes

rfc5997.description:
When enabled, this parameter allows the Instant AP to send a status-server request to determine the actual status of the authentication or accounting server. This proves useful when there is a authentication or request time
rfc5997—RFC5997 support enabled for both authentication and accounting on the authentication server.
auth-only—RFC5997 support enabled for authentication only.
acct-only—RFC5997 support enabled for accounting only
no rfc5997—Disables RFC5997 support for the authentication server.

ArubaAuthSurvivability_AuthSurvivability.description:
Configure the paramaters of authentication survivability. The authentication survivability feature requires ClearPass Policy Manager 6.0.2 or later,
and is applicable only when external servers such as RADIUS are configured for the SSID. When enabled, AP authenticates the previously connected clients using
EAP-TLS or MAC authentication even when connectivity to ClearPass Policy Manager is temporarily lost. The authentication survivability feature is not applicable when
a RADIUS server is configured as an internal server. This feature is only applicable for GW.

valid-from.x-typeDescription:
A date and time, expressed in the format described in RFC3339.
That is to say:

YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ+-hh:mm

where YYYY is the year, MM is the month expressed as a two-digit
month (zero padding if required), DD is the day of the month,
expressed as a two digit value. T is the literal character 'T',
HH is the hour of the day expressed as a two digit number, using
the 24-hour clock, MM is the minute of the hour expressed as a
two digit number. Z is the literal character 'Z', followed by a

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
The ipv4-address type represents an IPv4 address in
dotted-quad notation.  The IPv4 address may include a zone
index, separated by a % sign.
The zone index is used to disambiguate identical address
values.  For link-local addresses, the zone index will
typically be the interface index number or the name of an
interface.  If the zone index is not present, the default
zone of the device will be used.
The canonical format for the zone index is the numerical
format

The ipv6-address type represents an IPv6 address in full,
mixed, shortened, and shortened-mixed notation.  The IPv6
address may include a zone index, separated by a % sign.
The zone index is used to disambiguate identical address
values.  For link-local addresses, the zone index will
typically be the interface index number or the name of an
interface.  If the zone index is not present, the default
zone of the device will be used.
The canonical format of IPv6 addresses uses the textual
representation defined in Section 4 of RFC 5952.  The
canonical format for the zone index is the numerical
format as described in Section 11.2 of RFC 4007.

ArubaEst_EstProfilesSchemaGET.description:
Configurate the parameters of Enrollment over Secure Transport(EST) Profile. EST supports automatic enrollment of certificates with the EST Server. The certificates can be enrolled or re-enrolled automatically by
configuring an EST profile on the device. Certificate Enrollment with EST allows users to use their own PKI instead of the factory or self-signed certificates available on the Instant AP. This enables the user to
have maximum visibility and control over the management of the PKI used and address any issues related to security by themselves in a scaled environment.This feature is applicable for all devices.

profile.description:
Configurate the parameters of Enrollment over Secure Transport(EST) Profile. You can configure parameters such as server-host, server-port,
arbitrary-label, etc.
For AP, one EST profile is supported for per device.
For CX device, maximum of 16 profiles supported.

Arbitrary Label used in EST enrollment/reenrollment operations.
For AP device, valid length: 1-63 characters.
For CX device, valid length: 1-64 characters.

arbitrary-label-enrollment.description:
Arbitrary Label used in EST enrollment.
For Gateway device, valid length: 1-63 characters.
For AP device, valid length: 1-63 characters.

arbitrary-label-reenrollment.description:
Arbitrary Label used in EST reenrollment.
For Gateway device, valid length: 1-63 characters.
For AP device, valid length: 1-63 characters.

challenge-password.description:
Challenge Password used in EST enrollment. This configuration is valid only if
username is not configured.
challenge-password.x-typeDescription:
A custom derived type for special use cases. This type takes a plaintext password and uses
Vault's 3rd party API to encrypt the password. The intended use case is to encrypt and store
customer credentials which will be used later to login to 3rd party services.

csr-attribute.description:
CSR Attribute used in EST enrollment.
Following values are valid for AP and Gateway devices:
1. RSA_SHA256: RSA-2048 with SHA256 digest as CSR Attr value.
2. ECDSA_PRIME256V1_SHA256: ECDSA NIST P-256 with SHA256 digest as CSR Attr value
3. ECDSA_PRIME384R1_SHA384: ECDSA NIST P-384 with SHA384 digest as CSR Attr value
Below values are supported only for AP devices:
1. RSA_SHA384: RSA with SHA384 as CSR Attr value
2. RSA_SHA512: RSA with SHA512 as CSR Attr value

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

ArubaFirewall_FirewallSchemaGET.description:
Firewall monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic
based on predefined security rules. It protects against unauthorized
access, cyberattacks, and malicious threats. Firewall is superset of
several of its submodules which all together help in keeping traffic
secure. This model defines the Aruba firewall profile hierarchy used
by APs and Gateways to enforce stateful packet inspection and
policy-based traffic controls. It organizes firewall configuration
into reusable profiles with separate IPv4 and IPv6 subtrees, and
exposes tunables for session handling, traffic classification, rate
limiting/mitigation controls, multicast handling, and other datapath
behaviors.

profile.description:
A named firewall profile that encapsulates a complete set of IPv4 and
IPv6 firewall policies for a given deployment context. Only a single
firewall profile instance is permitted per scope. Each profile is
identified by a unique name and contains separate IPv4 and IPv6
containers with tunables for session management, traffic classification,
spoofing protection, multicast optimization, and various datapath behaviors.
Profiles can be created, updated, and deleted independently, allowing
administrators to maintain multiple policy sets and apply them to different
device groups or network segments as needed.

prevent-dhcp-exhaustion.description: Enable check for DHCP client hardware address against the packet source MAC address. This command checks the frame's source-MAC against the DHCPv4 client hardware address and drops the packet if it does not match. Enabling this feature prevents a client from submitting multiple DHCP requests with different hardware addresses, thereby preventing DHCP pool depletion.

prohibit-arp-spoofing.description: Detects and prohibits arp spoofing. When this option is enabled, possible arp spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent.

prohibit-ip-spoof-all.description: Detects ARP spoofing, when an intruder sends ARP using the IP and MAC addresses of a known user. When this option is enabled, additional check for the user route cache entry is performed. If the route cache entry is not found or if found, but the route cache entry MAC does not match with the sender MAC in ARP frame, then, the frame is marked as spoof. The IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. If the Prohibit IP Spoofing option is enabled, the controller denies all the traffic from the client using an IP address that is used by another client that has an entry in the user table. This option does not allow multiple MAC addresses to use the same IP address.

prohibit-ip-spoofing.description: Detects IP spoofing (where an intruder sends messages using the IP address of a trusted client). When this option is enabled, source and destination IP and MAC addresses are checked; possible IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. Enabled in IPv4, disabled in IPv6.

prohibit-rc-update.description: This option prohibits route-cache update on user add. Disabled by default.

prohibit-rst-replay.description: Closes a TCP connection in both directions if a TCP RST is received from either direction. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Disabled by default

restrict-corp-access.description: Restricted access to the corporate network.

This command checks the frame's source-MAC against the DHCPv4 client hardware address and drops the packet if it does not match. Enabling this feature prevents a client from submitting multiple DHCP requests with different hardware addresses, thereby preventing DHCP pool depletion.

prohibit-arp-spoofing.description: Detects and prohibits arp spoofing. When this option is enabled, possible arp spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent.

prohibit-ip-spoof-all.description: Detects ARP spoofing, when an intruder sends ARP using the IP and MAC addresses of a known user. When this option is enabled, additional check for the user route cache entry is performed. If the route cache entry is not found or if found, but the route cache entry MAC does not match with the sender MAC in ARP frame, then, the frame is marked as spoof. The IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. If the Prohibit IP Spoofing option is enabled, the controller denies all the traffic from the client using an IP address that is used by another client that has an entry in the user table. This option does not allow multiple MAC addresses to use the same IP address.

prohibit-ip-spoofing.description: Detects IP spoofing (where an intruder sends messages using the IP address of a trusted client). When this option is enabled, source and destination IP and MAC addresses are checked; possible IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. Enabled in IPv4, disabled in IPv6.

prohibit-rc-update.description: This option prohibits route-cache update on user add. Disabled by default.

prohibit-rst-replay.description: Closes a TCP connection in both directions if a TCP RST is received from either direction. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Disabled by default

restrict-corp-access.description: Restricted access to the corporate network.

session-idle-timeout.description: Time, in seconds, that a non-TCP session can be idle before it is removed from the session table. You should not modify this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Default value is 16. Valid range 16-300

session-spread.description: Enables counter CPU to perform encryption. Applicable to 7200 Series controllers only Disabled by default

session-tunnel-fib.description:
Enable session,tunnel based forwarding. !!Warning!! It
is recommended to toggle this knob during maintenance
window or OFF peak production hours. On M3 this knob
will enable ONLY tunnel based forwarding, session based
does NOT apply to this platform.

shape-mcast.description: Enables multicast optimization and provides excellent streaming quality regardless of the amount of VLANs or IP IGMP groups that are used. Disabled by default.

stall-crash.description: Triggers datapath crash on stall detection. Applies to the to 7200 Series managed device only

tcp-session-idle-timeout.description: Time, in seconds, that a TCP session can be idle before it is removed from the session table. You should not modify this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Default value is 16. Valid range 300-43200

track-spoof.description: Detects spoof in datapath. Disabled voip-qos-trusted Prioritizes the RTP traffic based on the DSCP value set by the end user device. NOTE: On enabling, all UCC based ALGs will be disabled. Disabled by default.

tunnel-trusted.description:
Changes the role of incoming tunnel traffic in the inbound firewall role to a permit-all role.
Enabling this parameter allows the AP to be remotely managed through the secured tunnel with the VPN concentrator.

voip-wmm-content-enforcement.description: If traffic to or from the user is inconsistent with the associated QoS policy for voice, the traffic is reclassified to best effort and data path counters incremented. This parameter requires the PEFNG license. Disabled by default

wireless-bridge-aging.description: Prevent the age-out of wireless clients when associated to AP. Enabled by default.

attack-rate.description:
List of attack-rate protocol, rate and action configurations. Sets rates which, if exceeded, can
indicate a denial of service attack.

protocol.description: Protocol to monitor for Denial of Service attacks.

rate.description: Number of requests per 30 seconds. Valid range 1-16384

drop-ip-fragments.description: When enabled, all IP fragments are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

enable-per-packet-logging.description: Enables logging of every packet if logging is enabled for the corresponding session rule. Normally, one event is logged per session. If you enable this option, each packet in the session is logged. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative, as doing so may create unnecessary overhead on the managed device.

enable-stateful-icmp.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

enforce-tcp-handshake.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

enforce-tcp-sequence.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

ext-hdr-parse-len.description: Set the threshold value beyond which the IPv6 header will not be parsed and the packet will be dropped. Default value 100. Range 100-300

ArubaNetGroup_NetGroupsSchemaGET.description:
Configures network group (netdestination) profiles on the
device. A netdestination is a reusable named object that
defines a set of network destinations for use in firewall
policies and session ACLs. When an ACL rule references a
netdestination by name as a source or destination alias,
traffic is matched against all entries in that group.
Each network group can contain entries of type host (single
IP), FQDN (domain name), address-range (IP range), network
(subnet prefix), VLAN (VLAN-based override), port (protocol
port or port range), or interface (tunnel or null interface).
Additional features include inversion (match all destinations
except those in the group) and exclusion (subtract entries
of another netdestination from this group). Supported on
AP, Gateway, SW_CX and SW_PVOS platforms.

net-group.description:
A network group (netdestination) profile. Each profile
is identified by a unique name and contains a list of
network destination entries.

description.description:
A user-defined text description for this network group
profile, used for administrative identification.

exclude.description:
Name of another netdestination profile whose entries should
be excluded (subtracted) from this network group. When
specified, destinations matching the excluded profile are
removed from the effective match set of this group.

invert.description:
When set to true, inverts the match logic of this network
group. Traffic matching any destination NOT in this group
will match the ACL rule referencing this alias. Default
is false (normal match behavior).

items.description:
Ordered list of network destination entries within this
network group profile. Each entry defines a specific
network destination (host, FQDN, range, network, VLAN,
port, or interface) identified by a positional index.

address.description:
A single host IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) for this
network destination entry. Applicable when type is HOST.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

address-range.description:
A contiguous IP address range defined by exactly two
elements: the start address and the end address.
Applicable when type is ADDRESS_RANGE.

items.description:
A contiguous IP address range defined by exactly two
elements: the start address and the end address.
Applicable when type is ADDRESS_RANGE.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

fqdn.description: A Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) applicable when type is FQDN.

index.description:
Positional index of this entry within the network group.
Entries are evaluated in index order. Valid range is
1 to 1000.

network-vlan.description:
The VLAN ID used for network-level VLAN-based destination
matching. Specifies a network VLAN identifier (1-4094).
Applicable when type is VLAN.

ports.description:
Operator and port values. If operator == COMPARISON_RANGE then minimum and maximum values are valid,
otherwise only the minimum value is valid.

max.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

min.description: Port value or lower bound of port range.
min.x-typeDescription:
A 16-bit port number used by a transport protocol such as TCP
or UDP.

operator.description: Comparison operator.

x-enumDescriptions.COMPARISON_RANGE: Minimum and maximum values of range.

prefix.description:
A network subnet specified as an IP prefix (address and
prefix length). Applicable when
type is NETWORK.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 prefix represented in dotted quad notation followed by
a slash and a CIDR mask (0 <= mask <= 32).

An IPv6 prefix represented in full, shortened, or mixed
shortened format followed by a slash and CIDR mask
(0 <= mask <= 128).

type.description:

and INTERFACE requires 'null-interface' or 'tunnel-name'.

x-enumDescriptions.NETWORK: A network subnet defined by an IP address and prefix length.
x-enumDescriptions.VLAN:

traffic based on VLAN ID with an optional host offset.

ArubaPasspointIdentity_PasspointIdentity.description:
This is used to define a Network Access Identifier (NAI) realm information that
can be sent as an Access network Query Protocol (ANQP) information element in a GAS query response.
The settings configured in this profile determine the NAI realm elements that are included as part of a GAS Response frame.

profile.description:
List of NAI realms whose information can be sent as
an ANQP information element in a GAS query response.

anqp-3gpp.description: List of 3GPP Cellular Network for hotspots that have roaming relationships with cellular operators.

plmn.description: The Public Land Mobile Networks (PLMN) value of the highest-priority network.

items.description: The Public Land Mobile Networks (PLMN) value of the highest-priority network.

anqp-roam-cons.description: List Roaming Consortium OI information be sent in an ANQP information element in a GAS query response.

anqp-roam-cons-name.description: ANQP Roaming Consortium OI information profile name.

org-id.description:
Sends the specified roaming consortium OI in a GAS query response.
The OI must be a hexadecimal value.

auth-param.description: Use the nai-realm-auth-id to send the one of the nai_realm_auth_id methods for the primary NAI Realm ID.

id.x-typeDescription: The enum define of hotspot nai-realm-auth-id.

id-value.description:
key for module. This key is the combination of id and value separated by ~
id        - NAI Realm Authentication Parameter ID.
value     - NAI Realm Authentication Parameter value.

value.description:
NAI Realm Authentication Parameter value. The value need to pair to auth-id:
auth-id                      | auth-value scoped
-----------------------------|-------------------
RESERVED_NAI_REALM_AUTH_ID   | All nai_realm_auth_value
EXPANDED-EAP                 | All nai_realm_auth_value
NON-EAP-INNER-AUTH           | nai_realm_auth_value should in [NON_EAP_RESERVED - NON-EAP-MSCHAPV2]
EAP-INNER-AUTH               | nai_realm_auth_value should in [EAP-IDENTITY - EAP-PEAP-MSCHAPV2]
EXP-INNER-EAP                | All nai_realm_auth_value
CREDENTIAL                   | nai_realm_auth_value should in [CRED-SIM - CRED-VENDOR-SPEC]
TUNNELED-EAP-CREDENTIAL-TYPE | nai_realm_auth_value should in [TUN-CRED-SIM - TUN-CRED-VENDOR-SPEC]
value.x-typeDescription: The enum define of hotspot nai-realm-auth-value.

index.description: Index of EAP Auth Method list.

method.description: Select one of the options to identify the EAP authentication method supported by the hotspot2 Realm.
method.x-typeDescription: The enum define of hotspot nai-realm-eap-method.

enable-alias.description:
The user may apply an alias named 'enable-alias' for device specific practical config when no enable
is configured, allowing the user to control the profile enablement.

encoding.description:
Issue this command if the NAI Realm named
defined by nai-realm-name <nai-realm-name> is
a UTF-8 formatted character string that is not
formatted in accordance with IETF RFC 4282.
encoding.x-typeDescription: The enum define of hotspot nai-realm-enc.

home-realm.description: Marks the Realm in this profile as the NAI Home Realm.

identity-type.description: Type of authentication used for AirPass.

nai-realm-name.description: List of names for the NAI realm. The realm name is often the domain name of the service provider.

value.description: Value of the NAI realm name.

ArubaPortSecurity_PortSecuritySchemaGET.description:
Port security enables a user to configure each switch port with a
unique list of the MAC addresses of devices that are authorized to
access the network through that port. This security enables individual
ports to detect, prevent, and log attempts by unauthorized devices to
communicate through the switch.

name.description: Name of the port security policy.
Name of the port security policy.
Name of the port security policy.

ArubaRadiusModifiers_AttributeProfile.description:
This feature is to provide configuration commands to the user to include specific attributes in these access-request and the corresponding values of these attributes.
Including these attributes in access-request packets helps administrators assign appropriate access policies to the clients based on these attributes.

framed-ip-address.description:
This command enables the inclusion of the RADIUS attribute Framed-IP-Address (type 8) in RADIUS access request packets for port-access clients.
By default, the IP address assigned to the client is not included in the RADIUS access request packets. They are however included in the accounting packets.

request-type.description: RADIUS request type for Framed-IP-Address. This field can only be set if request-type is AUTHENTICATION.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Authentication & Accounting requests.

service-type.description: RADIUS service type for Framed-IP-Address. This field can only be set if service-type is PORT_ACCESS.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Management users and port-access clients authentication/accounting.

nas-identifier.description:
Configure the Network Access Switch Identifier.NAS-Id will be sent in RADIUS access-request and accounting packets, which is used to notify
the source of RADIUS access request. NAS-Id can be a FQDN of the NAS or any unique string to identify the NAS.

request-type.description: RADIUS request type for NAS Identifier.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Authentication & Accounting requests.

value.description: NAS Identifier value.

nas-ip-address.description:
Configuration to include Network Access Switch IP Address attribute in RADIUS access request packet.
By default NAS-IP-Address attribute will not be added in authentication or accounting packet for management users.
Both request-type and service-type should be set to include the NAS-IP-Address Attribute.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Authentication & Accounting requests.

service-type.description: RADIUS service type for NAS-IP-Address. This field can only be set if service-type is MANAGEMENT.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Management users and port-access clients authentication/accounting.
Authentication & Accounting requests.

value.description: Tunnel private group ID value.

x-enumDescriptions.DYNAMIC: VLAN assigned to the client by authentication server.
x-enumDescriptions.STATIC: Native VLAN of the client port.

vsa.description: This configuration allows a user to include specific VSAs in RADIUS request packets for different service types.

vendor.description: Name of the vendor, vsa-type and vsa-value must also be configured.

vendor-vsa-type.description: Key combination of vendor and vsa-type separated by ~

ArubaRadiusModifiers_AttributeProfileGet.description:
This feature is to provide configuration commands to the user to include specific attributes in these access-request and the corresponding values of these attributes.
Including these attributes in access-request packets helps administrators assign appropriate access policies to the clients based on these attributes.

framed-ip-address.description:
This command enables the inclusion of the RADIUS attribute Framed-IP-Address (type 8) in RADIUS access request packets for port-access clients.
By default, the IP address assigned to the client is not included in the RADIUS access request packets. They are however included in the accounting packets.

request-type.description: RADIUS request type for Framed-IP-Address. This field can only be set if request-type is AUTHENTICATION.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Authentication & Accounting requests.

service-type.description: RADIUS service type for Framed-IP-Address. This field can only be set if service-type is PORT_ACCESS.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Management users and port-access clients authentication/accounting.

nas-identifier.description:
Configure the Network Access Switch Identifier.NAS-Id will be sent in RADIUS access-request and accounting packets, which is used to notify
the source of RADIUS access request. NAS-Id can be a FQDN of the NAS or any unique string to identify the NAS.

request-type.description: RADIUS request type for NAS Identifier.

x-enumDescriptions.BOTH: Authentication & Accounting requests.

value.description: NAS Identifier value.

nas-ip-address.description:
Configuration to include Network Access Switch IP Address attribute in RADIUS access request packet.
By default NAS-IP-Address attribute will not be added in authentication or accounting packet for management users.
Both request-type and service-type should be set to include the NAS-IP-Address Attribute.

ArubaUbt_UbtSchemaGET.description:
Configuration of UBT (User based Tunnel) Profiles.
This feature creates UBT GRE tunnel between the
switch and the controller when UBT users are
present on the switch. It encapsulates incoming
packets from end-hosts in GRE and forwards them
to the Mobility Controller.The feature is enabled
on a Per User Tunneled Node basis.

profile.description:
A list of global profile(s) for UBT, each
scope (global, site, site-collection, device, device-collection)
can accept only one profile.

client-vid.description:
This vlan is used when mode is LOCAL_VLAN.
If UBT Client VLAN is configured in VLAN_EXTEND mode, it is ignored.
VLAN-ID assigned to UBT clients for tunneling traffic from
switch to controller.
client-vid.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

mode.description: UBT VLAN mode configuration

x-enumDescriptions.LOCAL_VLAN:
Clients are assigned to a VLAN that is local to
the switch and associated with their UBT-role
based VLAN when client traffic reaches the
controller. This mode allows for reducing the
number of VLANs that need to be instantiated on
the switch but can only support VLAN-untagged UBT
clients. The 'client-vid' will be used to
specify the local_vlan that UBT clients are
assigned to.
x-enumDescriptions.VLAN_EXTEND:
Clients are assigned to their UBT-role based
VLAN in the hardware datapath. This mode allows
for UBT to support VLAN-tagged clients like VOIP
phones.

name.description: UBT profile name to be configured.

zone.description: A list of UBT zone specific configuration.

backup-controller-ip.description:
UBT zone's secondary controller's ip address.
Each zone within a profile must have a unique backup-controller ip.
This ip must also be distinct from primary-controller ip within
the same zone and primary-controller ip of other zones
backup-controller-ip.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

enable.description: Enables/Disables UBT functionality for this zone.

maintenance-period.description:
The user-based tunnel maintenance period is in the range of
1 to 720 hours. The default value of 0 can be used to
disable the maintenance window. If maintenance period is configured
then authenticated clients will be retained in current role in the
event of controller unreachability. Client traffic will be dropped
in switch ingress port. Once controller is reachable, client
traffic flow will be resumed. If controller is not reachable even
after configured maintenance period, clients will be
deauthenticated.

papi-security-key.description:
Shared security key that will be used to encrypt UBT PAPI messages
exchanged between this switch and the controller cluster corresponding
to this zone. When not set, shared security key is not used for
encrypting papi messages.

primary-controller-ip.description:
UBT zone's primary controller's ip address.
Each zone within a profile must have a unique primary-controller ip.
This ip must also be distinct from backup-controller ip within
the same zone and backup-controller ip of other zones
primary-controller-ip.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

heartbeat messages to the Switch Anchor Controller(SAC).

keep-alive messages sent to the User Anchor Controller(UAC).

ArubaAirgroupPolicy_AirgroupPoliciesSche.description:
An Airgroup policy must have a service definition, whereas VLAN and roles are optional.
In case of roles, both 'allowed-roles' and 'disallowed-roles' cannot be
configured at the same time. One of them must be empty. A maximum of 20 roles can be configured.
In case of VLANs, both 'allowed-vlans' and 'disallowed-vlans' cannot be
configured at the same time. One of them must be empty. A maximum of 20 VLANs or VLAN ranges
can be configured.
This feature is applicable for AP.

policy.description: List of policies for each Airgroup service to be applied at different scope.

name.description: Name of the Airgroup service. This should refer to one of the pre-defined services or a custom-service that has been defined by user.

server-expiry-time.description:
Duration in minutes after which the records
of inactive servers are purged. This timer will be used for
all server records belonging to this service. Allowed range
is from 60 (1 hour) to 360 (6 hours). If this is not
configured, the records are purged as per TTL/max-age specified
in packets

ArubaAirgroupServiceDefinition_AirgroupS.description:
A Airgroup service definition is a group of service ID(s), which requires
at least one custom service ID. A service ID can be of type mDNS or SSDP.
A maximum of 100 service IDs are allowed across all the services.
A maximum of 16 services are allowed and in each service 32 service IDs are allowed.
There are pre-defined services with default service IDs. These are read-only and
can be enabled or disabled. This feature is applicable for AP

ArubaLocation_LocationSchemaGET.description:
Location configuration. It supports three methods for locating:
1, Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI): Calculate the pathloss of signal to locate a device.
2, Analytics and Location Engine (ALE): The ALE is designed to gather client information from
   the network, process it, and share it through a standard API. The client information
   gathered by ALE can be used for business purposes by analyzing a client’s Internet behavior
   such as shopping preferences.
   ALE includes a location engine that calculates the associated and unassociated device
   location every 30 seconds by default.
3, Real Time Location System (RTLS): AP supports the real-time tracking of devices
   when integrated with the Airwave server or a third-party RTLS server such as
   Aeroscout RTLS server. With the help of the RTLS, the devices can be monitored in
   real time or through history.

This feature is only applicable for AP.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 prefix represented in dotted quad notation followed by

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
An IPv4 address in dotted quad notation using the default
zone.

An IPv6 address represented as either a full address; shortened
or mixed-shortened formats, using the default zone.

The domain-name type represents a DNS domain name.
Fully quallified left to the models which utilize this type.

Internet domain names are only loosely specified.  Section
3.5 of RFC 1034 recommends a syntax (modified in Section
2.1 of RFC 1123).  The pattern above is intended to allow
for current practice in domain name use, and some possible
future expansion.  It is designed to hold various types of
domain names, including names used for A or AAAA records
(host names) and other records, such as SRV records.  Note
that Internet host names have a stricter syntax (described
in RFC 952) than the DNS recommendations in RFCs 1034 and
1123, and that systems that want to store host names in
schema nodes using the domain-name type are recommended to
adhere to this stricter standard to ensure interoperability.

The encoding of DNS names in the DNS protocol is limited
to 255 characters.  Since the encoding consists of labels
prefixed by a length bytes and there is a trailing NULL
byte, only 253 characters can appear in the textual dotted
notation.

Domain-name values use the US-ASCII encoding.  Their canonical
format uses lowercase US-ASCII characters.  Internationalized
domain names MUST be encoded in punycode as described in RFC
3492

ArubaApSystem_ApSystemSchemaGET.description:
Manage global system settings for Aruba Access Points, including time zone,
location, cluster mode, LED control, and operational parameters. These configurations
define device identity, network integration, security policies, and system-wide behaviors
such as country code, virtual controller settings, and advanced features like CPU management
and thermal controls. This profile references Alias profiles for reusable configuration templates.
Use this API to retrieve the list of AP System profiles.

profile.description:
Defines a single AP System profile containing all system-level configurations for one or more
Access Points. Each entity is identified by name. Use these APIs to create, modify, or delete
an instance.

advanced-zone.description:
Enable or disable the advanced zone feature that can configure up to 32 SSIDs.
Since the mapping method of the WLAN index and BSSID index are different,
when you change the advanced zone configuration, the BSSID is removed and created again.
When advanced zone is enabled:
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 A zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 16 SSIDs.
 However, if the extended SSID is disabled,
 a zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 14 SSIDs wherein the first two virtual APs are reserved for mesh.

advertise-ap-health-ie.description:
Control AP to enable/disable 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature. This feature is enabled by default.
'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature controls AP to broadcast the AP health IE through the wireless SSIDs.
The AP health IE contains many flags that can reflect current AP status like uplink status,
Central connectivity status. Once AP lost Central connection, this AP health IE can be broadcast through
wireless beacons so that our Aruba APs nearby can hear this beacon and send the AP health IE to Central.
This will allow the user or engineer to understand the status of the issue AP and take measures to rescue it.

advertise-location.description:
Enable advertising location info in beacon frame.
Disable by default.

allow-new-aps.description: Allows the new access points to join the AP cluster. This API is AOS8 specific.

allow-new-aps-alias.description: Alias for allow new aps. This API is AOS8 specific

allowed-ap.description:
Specifies the MAC address of an AP permitted to join the cluster. Available on firmware versions up to 10.0.0.
This setting is specific to AOS8 platforms.

items.description:
Specifies the MAC address of an AP permitted to join the cluster. Available on firmware versions up to 10.0.0.
This setting is specific to AOS8 platforms.

Available on firmware versions 8.6.0 to 8.11.99 only.

cluster-security.description:

Enabling cluster-security dtls will form Datagram TLS connection between Conductor and Member APs.

allow-low-assurance-devices.description: Allow non-TPM (Trusted-Platform-Module) devices to connect over DTLS

dhcp-option82-xml.description:
Configure DHCP Option 82 XML file. The AP inserts circuit and remote ID information
into DHCP requests from clients.

x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_1_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 1. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: AP Name, AP MAC Address, Extended AP MAC Address,
Remote ID: User's MAC Address.
x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_2_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 2. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: AP MAC Address, Extended AP MAC Address, SSID Tunnel,
Remote ID: User's MAC Address.
x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT_DHCPOPT82_3_XML:
Default DHCP Option 82 XML file 3. Values for Circuit and Remote ID's are as follows:
Circuit ID: User's MAC Address,
Remote ID: AP Name, Extended AP MAC Address.

VLAN or VLAN range for which DHCP Option 82 XML applies. Allowed values: a single VLAN (1-4094)

disable-factory-reset.description:

down reset button for 5 seconds.

drt-upgrade-disable.description: Disable the automatic download and installation of DRT updates on the AP managed by Aruba Central.

dynamic-cpu-mgmt.description: Enable/Disable Dynamic CPU management to manage resources across different functions performed by an AP.

x-enumDescriptions.AUTO:
Configure the AP to automatically enable or disable CPU management feature during run-time.
When configured, the AP determines the need for enabling or disabling CPU management, based
on the real-time load calculations taking into account all different functions that the CPU
needs to perform. The auto option is the default and recommended setting.

Enable the CPU management feature. When configured, the client and network management functions
are protected. This setting helps in large networks with a high client density.

enet-vlan.description: Configures VLAN for the upstream switch to which the AP is connected.

extended-ssid.description:
This command allows you to configure additional WLAN SSIDs.
Extended SSID is enabled in the factory default settings of APs.

fips-enable.description:
Enable/Disable FIPS mode for AP. When enabled, AP operates in compliance with FIPS
and utilizes approved cryptographic algorithms and modules for enhanced security.
Note that toggling this knob will lead to a reboot of the AP.

firsthop-security.description:
Controls first hop security features on the AP. When enabled, security features are active.
Available on firmware versions 10.7.1 and later.
By default these security features are enabled on the AP.

ip-mode.description:
Selects the IP mode for packet processing.
IPV4_ONLY processes only IPv4 packets; IPV4_PREFER prioritizes IPv4 over IPv6.

x-enumDescriptions.IPV4_ONLY: Enables system processing of IPv4 packets.
x-enumDescriptions.IPV6_ONLY: Enables system processing of IPv6 packets. Not supported on Microbranch APs.

ip-mode.x-typeDescription: IP mode to process IPv6 or IPv4 packets.

itm.description:

AP will be throttled down to reduce its internal temperature. The limitations of AP operations
is defined by the priority assigned for reduction steps configured in Intelligent Power Monitoring(IPM)
API. IPM must be enabled for ITM to function.

advanced-zone.description:
Enable or disable the advanced zone feature that can configure up to 32 SSIDs.
Since the mapping method of the WLAN index and BSSID index are different,
when you change the advanced zone configuration, the BSSID is removed and created again.
When advanced zone is enabled:
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.
 A zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 16 SSIDs.
 However, if the extended SSID is disabled,
 a zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 14 SSIDs wherein the first two virtual APs are reserved for mesh.

advertise-ap-health-ie.description:
Control AP to enable/disable 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature. This feature is enabled by default.
'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature controls AP to broadcast the AP health IE through the wireless SSIDs.
The AP health IE contains many flags that can reflect current AP status like uplink status,
Central connectivity status. Once AP lost Central connection, this AP health IE can be broadcast through
wireless beacons so that our Aruba APs nearby can hear this beacon and send the AP health IE to Central.
This will allow the user or engineer to understand the status of the issue AP and take measures to rescue it.
